focus-productivity-6.territory: It is 8:52 in a classroom of 24 kids, or minute forty of a bedtime negotiation: the adult is stretched thin and the child cannot read a clock. The interface answers with instant legibility from across a room, one shape that IS the time, so calm that the timer never becomes more interesting than the task. Clarity here means a poster, not an app.

palette.note: The persimmon accent lives almost entirely inside the disk itself; all chrome stays chalk-neutral so nothing on screen competes with the time.

focus-productivity-6.typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible for every label (a typeface literally built for legibility, honest in a classroom), kept small and quiet because the disk is the typography and digits are hidden by default.
focus-productivity-6.motif: The whole-circle disk: any duration you pick fills the entire circle, so half the time always looks like exactly half the circle, no fractions, no clock math.

ia.coreObject: A timed moment: a single visual timer or one step inside a routine chain
ia.primaryLoop: Tap a duration or a chain, the disk fills full and shrinks while the child watches from anywhere in the room; mornings, transitions, and bedtimes repeat daily, so the timer does too.

invoice-maker-7.territory: A tradesperson between job sites, hands full, sun on the windshield, zero patience for admin. The interface answers with jobsite clarity: gloves-on tap targets, glance-legible numbers, and the quiet competence of a tool that already filed the trip to the right client before the truck door closed. It should feel like a well-organized van, not an accounting office.

palette.note: Safety orange means money, deductions earned and billable lines, while everything else stays in grayscale so the screen reads instantly in truck-cab sunlight.

invoice-maker-7.typography: IBM Plex Sans at heavy weights for glance-reading from a cupholder, with IBM Plex Mono for miles and dollars so every column lines up like a printed invoice.
invoice-maker-7.motif: The geofence stamp: every saved job site is a bold ring on a quiet map, and each visit punches the ring like a hole struck on a job card.

ia.coreObject: the trip, filed to a client
ia.primaryLoop: Drive the day as usual while arrivals at saved sites file themselves, then a ten-second evening swipe pass turns the day's driving into deductions and invoice lines.

journaling-mood-2.territory: The person opens the app in a fragile or flattened moment, sometimes at 2 am mid-episode, and the last thing they need is cheerfulness or friction. The interface answers with the privacy of a good paper ledger: cream, ink, quiet serif labels whose meaning never drifts. It feels permanent and exact, like a notebook a psychiatrist would trust.

palette.note: Ink on cream everywhere; the fountain-pen blue appears only as the pen itself, marking today's dots and the single primary action, never as decoration.

journaling-mood-2.typography: Tiempos Text for scale labels and headings, Söhne for numbers and interface chrome; the serif gives every level-word the fixed, printed authority of a form the doctor has seen a hundred times.
journaling-mood-2.motif: The ruled ledger line: each of the four scales is one horizontal rule with labeled stops, and today's state is a single ink dot pressed onto it, so a month reads as four steady lines of dots.

ia.coreObject: The daily entry: four labeled scale dots plus sleep hours and medications, exactly one per day
ia.primaryLoop: A 90-second evening check-in placing four dots and confirming meds; people come back because an unbroken ledger is what makes the next psychiatrist appointment actually work.

journaling-mood-4.territory: She opens it in the early morning or the last quiet minutes of the evening, carrying real weights: a father's biopsy, a daughter's move, a friend's marriage. The interface answers like a well-bound paper journal from a church bookstore: cream pages, ink, scripture set with reverence, and room for an answer to arrive months later. It never performs spirituality back at her; it keeps the record of a faith being practiced.

palette.note: Cream paper and warm ink with a single deep violet used like a ribbon and for the word 'Answered'; color never celebrates, it marks.

journaling-mood-4.typography: Adobe Caslon Pro for scripture and headings, Freight Text Pro for her own writing: a book voice, not an app voice, with verses set with true small caps and hanging quotes.
journaling-mood-4.motif: The ribbon: a thin violet satin bookmark hangs from the top edge of every screen, marking today's page, and moves when an old request is finally marked answered.

ia.coreObject: The request: a prayer with a date, the people it is for, and space for how it was answered
ia.primaryLoop: Morning verse and a look at open requests, three lines of gratitude in the evening; she returns because requests she planted months ago keep resolving, and the journal is where that becomes visible.

meal-prep-grocery-1.territory: It is Sunday afternoon and the user is trying to turn five recipe tabs into one trip to the store without buying a third bag of flour. The interface answers with the calm of a well-run kitchen: crisp lists, visible arithmetic, and the small satisfaction of watching two ingredient lines fold into one. Fresh and practical, never foodie-glossy.

palette.note: Market-fresh white with produce-green accents; green marks additions and merges, while 'have it at home' items fade to a soft strikethrough gray instead of disappearing, so the subtraction stays visible and trusted.

meal-prep-grocery-1.typography: Cabinet Grotesk for headings and day labels, Inter for list rows and quantities; friendly weight up top, utterly legible arithmetic below, like a good grocery receipt.
meal-prep-grocery-1.motif: The roll-up bracket: whenever ingredients merge, a thin green bracket visibly gathers the source recipe lines into the single combined line, keeping the math inspectable at a glance.

ia.coreObject: The week (a meal plan whose byproduct is one clean shopping list)
ia.primaryLoop: Pick recipes for the week, tap what's already at home, and walk the store with one deduplicated list; the growing recipe library and the shared plan with a partner are what bring both adults back every Sunday.

meditation-mindfulness-2.territory: Heart at 140, hands unsteady, a decision budget of about five seconds: the person cannot choose, read, or navigate. The interface answers with dusk-dark emptiness and exactly one thing happening, a slow amber horizon that breathes so they do not have to think about breathing. Everything else in the product exists to be configured earlier, in a calm hour, so the crisis screen can be almost nothing.

palette.note: Color barely moves: the warm amber horizon brightens on the inhale and settles on the exhale, and nothing else on screen changes at all.

meditation-mindfulness-2.typography: Söhne in exactly two sizes; during a protocol the type nearly disappears, one short line at a time, set large and low-contrast so it guides without demanding to be read.
meditation-mindfulness-2.motif: The dawn horizon: a soft amber band low on the screen that rises with every inhale and sinks with every exhale, the whole interface reduced to one slow tide.

ia.coreObject: A protocol: a pre-configured rescue scenario with a chosen voice, pace, and duration

notes-pkm-1.territory: Sunday evening, tea beside the iPad, the small ritual of setting up the week that Hobonichi people guard like a sacrament. The interface answers as a well-bound notebook would: it opens flat, stays quiet, and offers beautiful blank structure without ever selling another sheet of paper. The pleasure is in the tool disappearing under the pen.

palette.note: Warm cream paper under near-black ink, with Hobonichi vermillion appearing only as the printed grid accents and the current-day marker, exactly like red ink on a Japanese planner.

notes-pkm-1.typography: Tiempos Text for printed template labels and dates, set small and letterspaced like fine planner printing; the user's own handwriting is the real display face.
notes-pkm-1.motif: The stitched gutter: every spread has a true center seam with visible thread stitches, and pages turn around it with paper physics, so the app always reads as a bound book, never a canvas.

ia.coreObject: The notebook: a bound file of spreads (weekly, monthly, habit, budget) living as a document in iCloud
ia.primaryLoop: Open to this week's spread each morning, write plans and cross off yesterday in ink, and roll what is unfinished forward with one gesture on Sunday.

nutrition-calories-2.territory: The person logging is mid-flare or bracing for one, tired of being told it is stress, and quietly collecting evidence for a doctor who gets eleven minutes with them. The interface answers with clinical freshness: bright, unembarrassed, quick enough to use from a bathroom, and honest enough to say 'not enough data yet' out loud. It treats the gut like a system under study, not a failing.

palette.note: Clean white with a cool teal reserved for statistically confident findings; unconfirmed patterns stay grey so color itself encodes evidence.

nutrition-calories-2.typography: Söhne for interface text and Söhne Mono for timestamps and confidence figures, giving lab-report neutrality with warmth in the generous sizes.
nutrition-calories-2.motif: The delay arc: a thin arc that leaps across the day timeline from a food dot to a symptom dot, its span labeled 6h, 12h, or 24h, the app's entire thesis drawn as one line.

ia.coreObject: The day timeline: a single vertical strand holding food dots and symptom dots in true time
ia.primaryLoop: Two taps after eating, two taps when a symptom hits, then each Sunday the app surfaces which arcs kept repeating and the doctor report writes itself.

password-manager-1.territory: The user has finally decided to leave a password manager that holds 300 accounts hostage, and they are quietly afraid of losing even one. The interface answers with the dignity of a notary's office: warm paper, ledger rules, and numbers that reconcile in front of you. Nothing playful, nothing neon, just proof at every step that everything came across.

palette.note: Warm archival paper with deep-ink text; the bottle-green accent appears only where a count balances or an action is safe, and unparsed items use ink underlines, never alarm red, because loss here is information, not panic.

password-manager-1.typography: Source Serif 4 for headings and counts, Inter for UI labels and table cells; the serif carries certificate-grade gravity while tabular Inter keeps every reconciliation column honest.
password-manager-1.motif: The double-entry rule: every stage shows an 'in' figure and an 'out' figure joined by a hairline ledger rule, so the migration reads like a balanced book from start to finish.

ia.coreObject: The migration (one source file becoming one verified target file)
ia.primaryLoop: Drop an export file, watch fields map and counts reconcile, fix the stragglers, and walk away with a target file plus a report proving nothing was lost; most users come once, do the job, and leave satisfied, which is the point.

period-cycle-3.territory: She arrives wary, having just moved a decade of intimate medical history out of an app she no longer trusts, and she is checking whether this one deserves it. The interface answers like an archivist handing over the keys: calm, literate, adult, showing her the full record and the exit door in the same breath. Nothing pleads, nothing decorates, everything states.

palette.note: Warm archival paper with plum-black ink; the single garnet accent marks only what is hers to act on (export, backup, today), never decoration.

period-cycle-3.typography: Signifier for headings and cycle-day numerals, Söhne for interface text: the voice of a well-set medical memoir, literate and unhurried, with numerals large enough to read like facts rather than stats.
period-cycle-3.motif: The decade strip: her entire history rendered as one continuous horizontal band of cycle segments, like archival microfilm you can scroll back through ten years without a single chart.

ia.coreObject: The record: a single continuous, exportable cycle history that predates and outlives the app
ia.primaryLoop: She logs today in two taps, glances at where she is in the cycle, and returns because the record only stays complete if she keeps it, and the app keeps proving it stays hers.

personal-finance-1.territory: It is 9:40 pm on the sofa with a receipt still in the coat pocket: the user chose manual entry on principle, and the two seconds of typing the number is the whole ritual. The interface answers with the tactility of a well-made cash register in daylight, fast, physical, and done, so quiet competence comes from the act of entry rather than from dashboards.

personal-finance-1.typography: IBM Plex Mono for every number (tabular, columns always align, honest to the cent) with Inter for labels; the mono numerals carry the personality of a ledger, never a dashboard.
personal-finance-1.motif: The stamp: each saved entry lands with a small green ink-stamp mark, and every day you logged gets a stamped tick in the month ledger, so consistency is literally visible as ink.

personal-finance-2.territory: The person is standing at a register or hovering over a checkout button, mildly anxious, asking one question: can I afford this today. The interface answers with daylight certainty, one honest figure in warm morning light, math you can open like a receipt. No dashboard noise, no draining monthly balance, just today's number and the quiet satisfaction of watching yesterday's restraint slide into it.

palette.note: Color speaks only through the number itself, which shifts green, amber or red with the day's health, while the surrounding chrome never changes so the numeral is the entire weather report.

personal-finance-2.typography: GT America Mono carries every figure in tabular, unblinking digits while Untitled Sans handles the prose, so the daily number reads like an instrument and everything else stays out of its way.
personal-finance-2.motif: The rollover ribbon: at midnight, yesterday's unspent dollars slide under today's numeral as a thin folded paper strip docking into place, so discipline is literally seen adding itself to the day.

ia.coreObject: the day, a dated spendable number with its purchases attached
ia.primaryLoop: Check the number with morning coffee, log purchases in three taps as they happen, and come back at night to watch the leftover ribbon roll into tomorrow.

personal-finance-4.territory: It is the tenth of the month, the paycheck landed, and she is standing at her shelf of envelopes deciding what this month gets. The interface answers with daylight bookkeeping calm: flat paper pockets, exact figures, no charts and no commentary, the quiet competence of someone who has done this for years. Nothing here performs; a full envelope simply looks full.

palette.note: Cool daylight grey-green around white paper envelopes; the deep green ink is the fill inside envelopes and the confirm actions, so color literally is money allocated.

personal-finance-4.typography: Untitled Sans for interface text with all money set in Founders Grotesk Mono tabular figures: numbers align to the cent down every column, like a ledger kept by hand but never smudged.
personal-finance-4.motif: The paper pocket: every envelope is a flat white rectangle with a visible flap, filled from the bottom edge by a solid rising tint of green ink, so the whole month is readable as fill levels on a shelf.

ia.coreObject: The envelope: a named pocket with a balance, a limit, and its own refill schedule
ia.primaryLoop: She deducts a purchase from an envelope in two taps (often from the widget), glances at the shelf, and comes back because the shelf is the only true picture of what she can still spend.

personal-finance-8.territory: A self-employed person carries a low hum of tax dread all year: the shoebox of receipts, the miles nobody wrote down, the audit letter they imagine at 2 a.m. The interface answers with archival calm, everything filed the moment it happens, stamped, retrievable, backed by a document. Using it should feel like closing a filing-cabinet drawer that locks with a satisfying click.

palette.note: Archival blue marks only what is documented and deductible, while unclassified trips and receipts wait in gray until a swipe files them, so the screen itself shows how audit-ready you are.

personal-finance-8.typography: Atlas Grotesk sets the interface and Atlas Typewriter sets every amount, date and merchant line, giving each entry the fixed-width certainty of a record that has been officially filed.
personal-finance-8.motif: The perforated tear-line: every captured receipt and classified trip carries a punched perforation along its edge, the physical mark of a document that now exists in the vault and can be produced on demand.

ia.coreObject: the documented deduction, a trip or receipt with its proof attached
ia.primaryLoop: Drives log themselves in the background; the person swipes them business or personal at a red light and snaps receipts at the counter, and every swipe visibly grows the quarter's deduction total.

recipes-meal-planning-2.territory: The person is on the couch or standing at the counter with a 40-second TikTok they will absolutely lose by Friday, half-inspired and half-annoyed that the recipe exists only as narration. The interface answers with bright kitchen daylight and the satisfaction of a fair transcription: it did the listening, it shows its work frame by frame, and the video is suddenly a real document.

palette.note: Cool daylight neutrals let the video stills carry all the food color; tomato red is spent only on record-style moments — importing, confirming, saving.

recipes-meal-planning-2.typography: GT America for quantities and interface, Value Serif for recipe titles; titles read like a cookbook while everything around them reads like a fast kitchen tool.
recipes-meal-planning-2.motif: The frame-grab receipt: every extracted ingredient carries a tiny rounded still from the exact video moment it was heard or read, like a receipt proving where each line came from.

ia.coreObject: The captured recipe: ingredients and steps assembled from a video's narration, on-screen text, and caption, with the original video attached
ia.primaryLoop: Share a video from TikTok or Instagram, approve the extracted recipe in under a minute, cook from the collection on the weekend; the growing shelf of rescued recipes is the pull.

ride-hailing-1.territory: It is 11:40 pm, the driver is parked outside a closed mall deciding whether one more hour is worth it, tired of apps that guess. The interface answers with dashboard certainty: one hard number per hour, miles counted like an odometer counts them, nothing decorative between the driver and the money. Street energy, but the calm kind you feel when the meter is on your side.

palette.note: Asphalt black keeps glare off the windshield at night, and hi-vis road-marking amber is spent only on verified money and verified miles, never on chrome.

ride-hailing-1.typography: Barlow Semi Condensed for labels and headers with IBM Plex Mono tabular figures for every dollar and mile, so numbers line up like an odometer and read at a glance from a phone mount.
ride-hailing-1.motif: The lane dash: a dashed amber line, like highway paint, that runs under every verified figure and literally ticks segment by segment as background miles accrue.

sleep-tracking-3.territory: It is 2 a.m., the partner is snoring again, and the user is awake, resentful, and fumbling for a volume slider in the dark. The interface answers with the stillness of deep night: near-black indigo, moonlight-soft data, and the reassurance that the volume knob is now handled by something that never sleeps. Everything glows just enough to be read with one half-open eye.

palette.note: Deep-indigo night with a moon-silver accent; brightness is the information channel, the masking envelope literally glows brighter as it swells over a snore burst and dims back in silence, and nothing on the night screen exceeds candlelight luminance.

sleep-tracking-3.typography: Manrope in light and regular weights throughout; soft terminals and generous letterspacing keep even the morning numbers feeling like a whisper rather than a report card.
sleep-tracking-3.motif: The breathing envelope: a soft luminous band across the night timeline that swells over each covered snore burst and settles flat in silence, the product's entire behavior drawn as one calm shape.

ai-avatars-headshots-3.territory: The person has paid three other apps already and been handed a lighter, straighter-haired stranger every time — they arrive not excited but braced, ready to screenshot the next insult. The interface answers like a portrait photographer's studio calibrated on neutral gray: the UI recedes to nothing so skin reads true, and every promise is shown as measurement, not marketing. The feeling on delivery should be the exhale of finally being seen accurately.

palette.note: A true-neutral charcoal, deliberately unhued like a photographer's gray card so no cast contaminates how skin reads; warm bronze appears only on fidelity ticks and confirmations — color belongs to the photographs, not the chrome.

ai-avatars-headshots-3.typography: Neue Haas Unica in a whisper for all chrome so the UI stays backstage, with GT Alpina Fine for the few editorial moments — delivery headers and the fidelity report — where the product speaks.
ai-avatars-headshots-3.motif: The fidelity swatch: every generated shot carries a small paired chip — skin tone sampled from your source photo beside the tone sampled from the output — with a bronze tick when they match; the proof travels on the image itself.

ai-chatbot-1.territory: Week six of a story you have been telling with one character, and the quiet dread that tonight is the night they forget your name. The interface answers like a reading room after dark: focused, warm, and trustworthy, with the relationship's memory physically present at the edge of every conversation, a notebook you can always open and correct.

palette.note: Warm candlelight dark, no neon: amber marks only memory (pins, margin notes, the notebook spine), so anything glowing on screen is literally something remembered.

ai-chatbot-1.typography: Lora for the character's prose and every remembered fact, Inter for controls and metadata; the serif carries the story, the sans stays out of it, and the split itself teaches which words are the relationship and which are the app.
ai-chatbot-1.motif: The margin: a thin bound-notebook spine along the right edge of every chat where remembered facts surface as tappable margin notes at the moment they are created.

ia.coreObject: The relationship record: a fact base of who is who, what happened, and how it felt, living outside the chat log
ia.primaryLoop: Open to a card of where you left off, play tonight's scene, watch the margin catch what mattered, and correct the record when it gets something wrong.

ai-chatbot-6.territory: The user is a journalist or analyst about to put a claim in front of an editor or a client, and the fear is publishing something the model dreamed up. The interface answers with newsroom sobriety: every sentence arrives already fact-checked, stamped with a date, and honest about what it does not know. It feels like working with a careful researcher, not chatting with a mascot.

palette.note: Warm newsprint ground with black ink text; proofreader red is reserved exclusively for dates, source stamps and the honest 'no data' verdicts, so red always means verification, never alarm.

ai-chatbot-6.typography: Tiempos Text carries answers like a broadsheet column while Söhne Mono sets every date stamp, URL and search log, so prose reads as journalism and evidence reads as machinery.
ai-chatbot-6.motif: The dateline stamp: a small mono-set red chip (REUTERS · 14 MAR 2026) that sits before every sourced claim like a wire-service dateline, and its absence is itself information.

ia.primaryLoop: Ask a work question, read the answer with dates on every claim, open the passages that matter, and save the citation trail into the story or memo you are writing today.

ai-chatbot-8.territory: A small business owner opens this app under mild duress: a client is 60 days late, a lease needs signing Friday, a supplier shrugged off the last email. They feel out of their depth and worried about getting the wording wrong. The interface answers like a competent paralegal at a clean desk: procedural, unhurried, and honest about where a real lawyer is still required.

palette.note: Blue behaves like a fountain pen, appearing only on actions that commit something (generate, send, sign), while risk flags use a restrained amber so warnings read as counsel, not alarm.

ai-chatbot-8.typography: Source Serif 4 for document text so drafts look like finished legal paper, with Inter for the guided questions and UI chrome, never letting the two mix inside one block.
ai-chatbot-8.motif: The margin rule: a thin vertical line running down the left of every document with clause flags hung on it like a lawyer's redline margin, checkmarks for standard clauses, amber ticks for review-with-counsel.

ia.coreObject: The document, a drafted contract, demand letter or notice with its risk checklist and dispute thread attached
ia.primaryLoop: When a deal or dispute surfaces, pick the document type, answer the guided questions with the business profile pre-filled, send the export, and come back to log every reply into the thread.

ai-image-generation-3.territory: Someone about to make a permanent decision about their own body: equal parts thrill and cold feet, phone in one hand, sleeve rolled up. The interface answers like a good tattoo artist at a consult: unhurried, ink-black, honest about how the piece will really sit, never oversold. The image glows, the chrome disappears.

palette.note: Studio blackout so the skin photo is the only bright thing on screen; the violet of a thermal stencil transfer marks everything interactive, placement handles, active states, and nothing decorative.

ai-image-generation-3.typography: PP Right Grotesk gives display text the confident weight of flash-sheet lettering in normal case, while Neue Montreal handles controls, and all measurements render in tabular figures so 12.4 cm reads like a spec, not a caption.
ai-image-generation-3.motif: The stencil line: every selection, crop, and placement boundary is drawn as the thin violet outline of a thermal transfer stencil, the exact artifact a real artist presses onto skin before committing ink.

ia.coreObject: The placement: one design fitted onto one photo of your body, with real-world size
ia.primaryLoop: Shoot or import a body photo, drop a design on, nudge size and angle until it feels right, save the placement; people return each time a new idea or a client sketch lands.

ai-image-generation-4.territory: The artist is twenty frames into a series, and the dread is opening the next render to find the style has wandered. The interface answers like a well-run print studio after dark: a dim stage where only the artwork carries light, and a red seal that means this frame passed.

palette.note: The UI stays in violet-black shadow so frames carry all the light; vermilion appears only as the seal on frames that held the style, never as decoration.

ai-image-generation-4.typography: Space Grotesk carries the studio chrome with technical warmth; Space Mono sets seeds and generation parameters, so the reproducible parts of the craft look reproducible.
ai-image-generation-4.motif: The vermilion seal: a small hanko-style stamp pressed onto every frame that passed the style check — frames that drifted appear only as gray ghosts in the reject tray, unstamped and uncounted.

ia.coreObject: the project (a locked style, a character card, and its series of frames)
ia.primaryLoop: Open the current project, generate the next frames of the series, and keep only stamped, on-style work — returning because the series still looks like one hand drew it.

ai-image-generation-5.territory: The user is a handmade seller who has been burned: a generator once stretched their candle jar and misspelled their own label, and a buyer noticed. The tone hint says dark engine room, but this product's truth is the opposite: a bright studio cyclorama where the seller inspects their product like a photographer at a light table, because trust here is built by seeing every original pixel intact on neutral ground. The interface answers suspicion with proof.

palette.note: Studio-grey seamless backdrop with white work surfaces; the gaffer-tape blue is used only for the protection mask and its verdicts, so blue always means 'these pixels are untouchable'.

ai-image-generation-5.typography: Neue Haas Grotesk for the working interface with IBM Plex Mono for pixel counts, dimensions and verification verdicts, the language of a studio and the language of an inspection report.
ai-image-generation-5.motif: The sacred outline: a fine hatched blue boundary drawn tight around the product and its label text that never breaks, never animates away, and appears on every screen where generation happens.

ia.coreObject: The protected product: an original photo with a hard mask over the item and its text, plus every scene built around it
ia.primaryLoop: Photograph or import products, drop them into scenes where only the background renders, verify the pixel check, and export listing-ready shots in each marketplace's size, a storefront per evening.

ai-image-generation-6.territory: The person is holding the only photo of their grandmother that survived, or the one good shot from a shoot, and they are afraid the AI will hand back a stranger. The interface answers like a darkroom with the lights down: a black stage where the photograph is the only bright thing, and every tool announces exactly where it will and will not touch. It feels like surgery with the patient watching.

palette.note: Safelight red-orange is spent only on the boundary of consent: the live mask edge, the face-lock seal, and the unlock warning; the rest of the chrome stays achromatic so the photo owns all the color on screen.

ai-image-generation-6.typography: Söhne for the interface and Söhne Mono for coordinates, history steps and similarity scores: cool, technical restraint that lets the instruction field read like a note to a careful retoucher, not a magic spell.
ai-image-generation-6.motif: The safelight seal: every detected face wears a thin red-orange keyline with a small wax-seal lock at the chin that stays visibly intact through every edit, and breaking it requires a deliberate long-press that the app records in history.

ia.coreObject: The edit: one mask, one plain-language instruction, one before/after, all reversible
ia.primaryLoop: Bring in a photo, tap the thing that bothers you, say what should change in plain words, verify the before/after, and come back because the archive box still has forty more prints to save.

screens.title: Onboarding, step 1: the one promise
screens.purpose: State the contract before showing a single tool.
screens.hero: A family photo where a tapped jacket glows inside a safelight outline while both faces wear intact seals
screens.data: Copy: 'Only what you select gets changed. Faces are locked by default, always.' Sub-line: 'You can break a face lock only by hand, and we keep a record when you do.' Button: 'Show me'.

screens.title: Onboarding, step 2: tap to select
screens.purpose: Teach the single gesture on a sample image, mask building live.
screens.hero: A finger tap on a lamppost, the SAM2 mask blooming outward to its exact silhouette in 400 ms
screens.data: Caption: 'Tap anything. The selection finds its own edges.' Practice instruction pre-typed: 'remove the lamppost' with result shown strictly inside the outline, street behind it rebuilt. Footer: 'Drag the edge to grow or shrink the mask.'

screens.title: Studio, mid-edit
screens.purpose: The main screen in real use: a 1987 print scanned, background clutter selected, faces sealed.
screens.hero: The photograph full-bleed on black, a radiator behind the couple outlined in safelight, two face seals intact
screens.data: Instruction field: 'remove the radiator and continue the wallpaper pattern'. Status chip: 'Mask: 8.2% of frame · Faces: 2 locked'. Toolbar: tap-select, grow/shrink edge, instruction, history '3/10 steps'.

screens.title: Plain-language instruction
screens.purpose: The instruction moment: words in, change confined to the outline, nothing else negotiable.
screens.hero: The keyboard up, the mask pulsing gently to show exactly what the words will govern
screens.data: Typed: 'make the shirt navy blue, keep the fabric wrinkles'. Suggestion chips from the mask contents: 'recolor', 'remove', 'replace with...', 'clean stains'. Note under field: 'This applies to the selected shirt only. 2 faces remain locked.'

screens.title: Face lock, challenged
screens.purpose: The user taps a face by accident or intent: the app holds the line and explains the cost of crossing it.
screens.hero: The tapped face's seal brightening, a small sheet rising from the chin lock
screens.data: Sheet: 'This face is locked. Edits here can change who this person looks like.' Options: 'Keep locked (recommended)', 'Unlock this face — hold 2 seconds'. If unlocked, a permanent history entry is shown: 'Face unlocked by you · step 4'.

screens.title: Restoration mode
screens.purpose: Old-print workflow: damage repair across the frame with faces treated as evidence, not material.
screens.hero: A cracked 1962 print mid-heal, scratches dissolving zone by zone while both face seals hold
screens.data: Job card: 'Wedding portrait, scanned at 600 dpi · 14 damage zones found: 9 scratches, 3 stains, 2 tears'. Toggle: 'Repair inside faces: gentle mode (fills cracks, never redraws features)'. Progress: 'Zone 11 of 14'.

screens.title: Face similarity check
screens.purpose: The trust instrument: prove the restored face is the same person before saving is allowed.
screens.hero: Two face crops side by side, before and after, joined by a mono similarity readout
screens.data: Readout: 'Similarity: 0.97 — same person, within scanning noise'. Threshold note: 'Below 0.90 we flag the zone and offer to revert it.' One flagged example beneath: 'Left eye area 0.88 — tap to compare or revert this zone only'.

screens.title: Before / after slider
screens.purpose: The mandatory honest look before anything is saved.
screens.hero: A full-bleed vertical wipe handle across the photograph, original left, edited right
screens.data: Handle label: 'Feb 12 edit · 4 steps'. Beneath: 'Changed: radiator removed, shirt recolored, 9 scratches healed. Untouched: both faces, hands, window light.' Buttons: 'Save copy', 'Back to studio'. Saving without opening this screen is not possible.

screens.title: Edit history
screens.purpose: Ten lossless steps, each revertible alone, the audit trail as a feature.
screens.hero: A vertical film-edge strip of step thumbnails on the studio's left rail

ai-image-generation-7.territory: The user is a creator forty minutes from publishing, and the cover is the last thing between them and the upload button; they have been burned by diffusion typos and do not have $40 for a designer tonight. The interface answers as a backstage marquee shop: a dark stage where five glowing cover options hang under work lights, and the headline is a physical letterboard layer you can reach out and fix. Fast, showy where the art is, dead reliable where the words are.

palette.note: Neutral stage black without gradients lets the generated covers supply all the color; marquee yellow is spent only on the editable text layer and safe-zone guides, so yellow always means 'this part is yours to touch'.

ai-image-generation-7.typography: Archivo Expanded gives the app's own headers a marquee-poster confidence while General Sans handles controls, and the cover headlines themselves render in the user's brand fonts as true vectors.
ai-image-generation-7.motif: The peel: the headline lifts off the artwork at a slight angle like a letterboard panel whenever text is selected, physically proving that words live on their own layer above the image.

ia.coreObject: The layered cover: a generated artwork plane, a vector text plane, and a reserved face or logo zone, sized to one platform
ia.primaryLoop: Before each upload, describe the episode, pick one of five variants, straighten the headline in the safe zone, and export at platform size; the library remembers the show's look for next week.

ai-writing-5.territory: The author is 300,000 words into a series and quietly afraid the world is drifting underneath her, an eye color here, a river bank there. The interface answers like a well-kept card catalog: typographic, exact, quietly severe about what is canon and calm about everything else.

palette.note: The editor's oxblood is spent only on contradictions and canon seals, so a clean chapter reads almost colorless and a flagged one stings just enough.

ai-writing-5.typography: Ivar Text for card bodies and manuscript excerpts, Founders Grotesk for the catalog chrome, with contradictions underlined the way an editor's pencil would do it.
ai-writing-5.motif: The contradiction strip: a manuscript line and its canon card clipped together like two index cards under one paperclip, the drifting detail underlined in oxblood in both.

ia.coreObject: the canon card, one character, place, or rule of the world
ia.primaryLoop: After each writing session she pastes the new chapter in, clears the flags one by one, and files what the chapter just added to the canon.

ai-writing-6.territory: Someone with dyslexia or a year past a stroke, needing to answer a coworker in the next few minutes, holding a clear thought that refuses to come out in order. The frustration is not about eloquence — it is about being seen as capable. The interface answers with the dignity of a patient, competent scribe: warm paper calm, large certain type, and the promise made visible on every screen that the words that go out are the user's own, only assembled.

palette.note: Warm paper with high-contrast ink at WCAG AAA ratios; the iris violet marks exactly one thing — the connective words the tool added — so the user can always see where their voice ends and the glue begins.

ai-writing-6.typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible throughout, body at 19pt and the confirmation screen at 24pt; a typeface engineered for low-vision and dyslexic readers carries the product's entire promise before a single feature does.
ai-writing-6.motif: Fragments docking: loose text chips slide onto a single baseline and click flush into a sentence, with the added connectors typeset in iris so the assembly is always visible, never hidden.

ia.coreObject: The assembled message: the user's fragments plus visible connective tissue, awaiting explicit approval
ia.primaryLoop: Type or speak thoughts in whatever order they arrive, review the assembled sentence on the large confirmation screen, approve, send — and return because every message that went out sounded like them on a good day.

screens.title: Onboarding: turn the keyboard on
screens.purpose: Get through iOS keyboard setup with zero reading strain.
screens.hero: Three oversized illustrated steps, one per screen width, no paragraph text
screens.data: '1. Settings → General → Keyboard'. '2. Add New Keyboard → Assemble'. '3. Allow Full Access — assembly runs on your phone; your words don't leave it.' Text size slider shown live at 19pt with 'This is how big text will be'.

screens.title: Onboarding: how do your thoughts arrive
screens.purpose: Tune the input model to the person, not the other way around.
screens.hero: Three large cards with equal standing
screens.data: 'In pieces, typed' · 'Easier to say out loud' · 'Both, depends on the day'. Second question: 'Keep my words exactly (add only connectors) / Smooth spelling too'. Footnote: 'You can change this whenever. Hard days are allowed.'

screens.title: Keyboard in Messages, mid-thought
screens.purpose: The core surface: fragments going in, in any order, inside a real conversation.
screens.hero: The fragment tray above the keys holding four loose chips
screens.data: Conversation with 'Sandra (work)'. Chips in the tray: 'meeting moved' · 'cant do 3' · 'thursday works' · 'ask about room 4b'. One key glows softly: 'Assemble'. The chips are in the order typed, which is not the order they'll be said.

screens.title: The confirmation screen
screens.purpose: Show exactly what will be sent, large, before anything sends.
screens.hero: The assembled message at 24pt filling the upper half
screens.data: Assembled: 'The meeting got moved and I can't do 3, but Thursday works — could you ask about room 4B?' (connectors 'and', 'but', 'could you' in iris). Below, the original four chips unchanged. Buttons: 'Send this' · 'Fix a piece' · 'Start over'. Nothing sends without the tap.

screens.title: Reordering by hand
screens.purpose: Let the user drag chips when the tool guessed the wrong order.
screens.hero: A chip mid-drag, the sentence rewriting live beneath it
screens.data: User drags 'ask about room 4b' to first position; live result becomes 'Could you ask about room 4B? The meeting got moved…'. Hint: 'Drag pieces — the sentence follows you.' The tool's connectors re-fit around the new order in iris.

screens.title: Dictation mode
screens.purpose: Serve the days when speaking beats typing.
screens.hero: A single large record button with the live transcript arriving as chips
screens.data: Spoken: 'um tell the doctor the new pills… the dizzy thing is back… mornings mostly'. Chips formed: 'tell doctor about new pills' · 'dizziness is back' · 'mostly mornings'. Assembled preview: 'I wanted to tell the doctor that since the new pills, the dizziness is back — mostly in the mornings.' Same confirmation flow follows.

screens.title: Your words, proven
screens.purpose: Make the own-voice guarantee inspectable, not just claimed.
screens.hero: A two-column diff: fragments left, assembled right, additions in iris only
screens.data: Stats for the last message: 'Your words kept: 14 of 14 · Added: 5 connectors, 2 punctuation marks · Replaced: 0'. Line: 'If we ever need to change one of your words to make grammar work, it's underlined and you approve it separately.'

screens.title: On-device privacy
screens.purpose: State plainly where sensitive text lives and dies.
screens.hero: A phone outline with the assembly loop drawn entirely inside it
screens.data: 'Assembly runs on this phone. Your fragments and messages are never uploaded, never used for training.' 'History lives here too — delete it anytime.' 'Full Access is required by iOS for any custom keyboard; here is exactly what we do and don't do with it' with a short plain list.

screens.title: Tired-day mode
screens.purpose: Lower the effort further when fatigue is winning.
screens.hero: One fragment expanding into three ready replies to choose from
screens.data: Input: single chip 'cant make it today'. Three options at 24pt: 'I'm sorry, I can't make it today.' / 'I can't make it today — can we find another day?' / 'Not going to manage today. Tomorrow?'. Tap one, confirm, sent. Toggle lives on the keyboard as a small moon icon.

screens.hero: One plan card typeset at the same 24pt as the confirmation screen
screens.data: '$8/month, or $60/year.' Plain line: 'Less than the $144/year grammar checker — and built for how your thoughts actually arrive.' Included: unlimited assembly, dictation, tired-day mode, on-device processing. Trial: '30 messages free, no timer.' Links: 'Restore purchase' · 'Price help for stroke-recovery programs — email us'.

screens.purpose: Give a safe rehearsal before the first real send.
screens.hero: A practice conversation clearly marked 'Nobody receives this'
screens.data: Prompt: 'Try it here. Type three pieces of anything — grocery thoughts count.' Sample chips a tester might type: 'milk' · 'the good bread' · 'ask tom if eggs'. Assembled: 'Milk, the good bread — and ask Tom if we need eggs.' Banner: 'This screen sends nothing. Ever.'

ai-writing-7.territory: Seven in the morning, coffee cooling, a person who calls themselves 'trying to write' opening the app with the small dread that today will be another blank day. The interface answers like a good writing desk: cream paper, a single typeset prompt waiting like an epigraph, and quiet evidence on the shelf that the pages are accumulating. Not a productivity cockpit — a morning ritual that makes starting smaller than the fear.

palette.note: Cream paper and soft ink for the writing surface; the marigold appears only where words accumulate — the progress ring, the growing spine, the streak — so warmth is always earned by writing.

ai-writing-7.typography: Literata for the prompt and the writing surface, Karla for counters and UI; the reader-grade serif makes the user's own draft look like a book page, which is half the motivation.
ai-writing-7.motif: The growing spine: every day that hits its word goal adds a visible millimeter to the current month's book spine on the shelf, so a writing habit literally becomes a shelf of books.

ia.coreObject: The daily page: today's prompt, the word goal, and whatever gets written on it
ia.primaryLoop: Open the morning prompt, write toward a 300-word goal on a clean page, watch the spine grow — and return tomorrow because the streak and the shelf make yesterday's effort visible.

ai-writing-8.territory: It's late, and the player is 1,200 messages into a story they've carried for four months, half novelist and half archivist, braced for the platform to forget their character's name again or speak lines in their hero's mouth. The interface answers like a private library after hours: dark ink-violet quiet, serif story text, and the tactile certainty of things under seal — what the player pins stays pinned, what they built stays theirs. Authority sits with the player, visibly, on every screen.

palette.note: Ink-violet dark with parchment-toned text for long reading; antique gold belongs solely to acts of player authority — seals on pinned facts, the character card border, the export — and never decorates the bot's output.

ai-writing-8.typography: Newsreader for the story stream, General Sans for chrome and controls; the serif makes months of roleplay read like a manuscript, while the player's own messages carry a slightly heavier weight than the bot's.
ai-writing-8.motif: The wax seal: pinning a fact stamps it with a small gold seal that only the player's thumb can place, edit, or lift — the physical mark of what the world must remember.

ia.coreObject: The world: one player-owned bundle of character card, pinned facts, story log, and the running chat
ia.primaryLoop: Play a scene, seal the facts worth keeping, and come back nightly because the world reopens exactly where and how the player left it — no amnesia, no stolen lines.

screens.title: Onboarding: your character card
screens.purpose: Establish who the player is and the lines the bot may never cross.
screens.hero: A gold-bordered card being filled, hard limits section visually distinct
screens.data: 'Name: Kaelen Voss'. 'Appearance: gray-eyed, burn-scarred left hand, travels light'. Hard limits (locked section): 'Never speaks or acts for Kaelen' · 'Never harms the fox familiar' · 'No romance unless I initiate'. Line: 'Hard limits are enforced, not suggested. Violations get caught and struck.'

screens.purpose: The nightly core: a long-running scene awaiting the player's move.
screens.hero: The serif story stream ending on the bot's line, cursor waiting in the player's box
screens.data: Header: 'Miren · message 1,204 · strict mode on'. Bot's last line: 'The ferryman studies the coin, then Kaelen's scarred hand. "The Court's debts died with the Court," he says, not moving from the rope.' Input placeholder: 'Kaelen's move — yours alone.' A thin gold pin rail runs along the right edge showing 3 seals in this chapter.

screens.title: Pinning a fact

astrology-10.territory: The person is a practicing astrologer or serious student sitting down with a planner, not a seeker looking for comfort — they schedule launches, difficult conversations and rest around transits the way a sailor works the tides. The night-sky reverence is real but it has to submit to the grid of a working calendar; the interface answers with the feel of a fine printed almanac: celestial, yes, but paginated, dated, and ready to sync. Wonder, filed correctly.

palette.note: Almanac cream and midnight ink like a printed ephemeris; oxblood marks only peak dates and active transits, the way important days were once circled in a farmer's almanac, with a thin aged-gold rule reserved for the current date line.

astrology-10.typography: GT Sectra carries transit names and interpretations with an engraved, bookish authority, while Atlas Grotesk sets dates and calendar chrome — the pairing of an old almanac's plates with a modern planner's grid.
astrology-10.motif: The star-peaked bracket: every transit is one drawn bracket spanning start to end with a small eight-pointed star at its exact peak — stacked brackets become the year, and the same bracket shape survives export into Google Calendar event titles.

ia.coreObject: The transit event — one aspect to your natal chart with a start, a peak, an end and two sentences of meaning
ia.primaryLoop: Scan the next few weeks of brackets each Sunday while planning, push the ones that matter into the planner where real life is scheduled, and return whenever a decision needs a date.

astrology-2.territory: A working astrologer is about to read a chart for a paying client, and one wrong degree would make the whole session worthless. They arrive alert and slightly suspicious, cross-checking everything. The interface answers like a brass observatory instrument: calibrated, unhurried, proud to show its own error bars.

palette.note: Gold is reserved for computed positions and verification marks only, so the eye learns that gold means a number the engine stands behind.

astrology-2.typography: Spectral for chart titles and interpretive labels, IBM Plex Mono for every degree, minute and second so positions align in columns like an ephemeris table.
astrology-2.motif: A finely graduated degree ring, ticked every arc minute like the limb of a brass sextant, that frames every chart wheel and reappears as a thin calibration strip on data rows.

ia.coreObject: The chart, a timestamped calculation with a verifiable position table behind every wheel

astrology-4.territory: The person arrives straight from a $150 reading, still half under its spell and half ashamed of the spend, wanting to believe but tired of forgetting who promised what. The interface answers with the gravity of a night ledger: candlelit gold on deep ink, ceremonial enough to honor the practice, exact enough to hold every reader to their own words.

palette.note: Gold marks the sealed and the sacred, verified outcomes glow gold, failed predictions fade to the gray of the ink, and nothing ever flashes red at the user.

astrology-4.typography: GT Alpina for prediction quotes and reader names, Suisse Int'l for dates and money: the sharp serif gives testimony its weight, the neutral grotesk keeps the accounting cold and clear.
astrology-4.motif: The wax seal: every prediction is sealed with a gold wax stamp on entry and can only be broken open on its check-in date, so the ledger fills with sealed and broken seals that tell the whole story at a glance.

astrology-5.territory: Someone just got home from a second date, or added a new friend's birthday to their notes, and they want to know what actually runs between the two of them. The mood is curious, a little giddy, privately serious. The interface answers not with night-sky mysticism but with the warmth of a letterpress love-letter: paper, ink, and two circles that overlap.

palette.note: Iris violet marks the connection itself, aspect lines, overlap zones, shared elements, while each person's own chart stays in neutral ink so the relationship is always the colored thing.

astrology-5.typography: Canela for names and the strongest-connection headlines, giving readings the voice of a well-set book, with Untitled Sans for aspect data and orbs.
astrology-5.motif: The vesica piscis: two thin-lined circles overlapping, one per person, with everything shared living in the lens between them, repeated from app icon to loading state to the share card.

astrology-6.territory: It is late, the room is dark, and she opens the app the way she would step outside to look at the moon: seeking a small nightly ritual with real weight to it. The interface answers with a hush of deep blue-black and hairline gold, more observatory than feed. Wonder, but disciplined: one prompt, one page, one moon.

palette.note: Gold is spent only on the moon itself and the words you write; everything else stays in blue-black, so the page always feels lit by moonlight.

astrology-6.typography: Cormorant Garamond for prompts and phase names, Spectral for journal body text: a serif pairing that makes the writing page feel like a bound night journal, not an app.
astrology-6.motif: The intention ring: a hairline gold circle around the moon that fills like the waxing moon itself and closes exactly at full moon, carrying your intention across the cycle.

ia.coreObject: the cycle (one new-moon-to-full-moon arc holding an intention, its entries, and a closing summary)
ia.primaryLoop: Open tonight's phase-keyed prompt, write one page, and watch the intention ring wax toward full moon.

screens.title: Your chart, once
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 1: capture birth data so prompts key to the personal chart, not the sun-sign horoscope.

screens.data: Born: Mar 3, 1994 · 11:42 pm · Portland, OR → 'Rising Virgo · Moon in Pisces · Sun in Pisces. Your prompts will be written for your rising sign, never a generic horoscope.'

astrology-7.territory: Someone opens their Human Design chart the way you would step into a planetarium: expecting wonder, braced for jargon. The interface answers with a night sky that explains itself, where every strange symbol is a star you can touch and it speaks plainly. For the practitioner checking gates at lunch, the same sky becomes an hourly instrument they have trusted for years.

palette.note: Deep indigo night with parchment-warm text; gold is reserved for whatever is alive right now, defined channels and the currently transiting gate, so the chart literally glows where the energy is.

astrology-7.typography: Canela for center names, gate titles and lesson headings, lending the material its ceremonial weight, with Söhne for explanations so the plain-language layer feels modern and unmystified.
astrology-7.motif: Constellation gates: the 64 gates of the bodygraph rendered as stars that brighten, dim and draw golden channel lines as real transits shift hour by hour, making the chart a living sky rather than a static diagram.

ia.coreObject: The bodygraph: a birth chart of centers, gates and channels where every element explains itself on tap
ia.primaryLoop: Practitioners open the app with morning coffee to see which gates the sky lit up today and get a chime when a gate changes; newcomers return for the next lesson until the same sky starts making sense.

screens.title: Onboarding: birth details
screens.purpose: Collect date, time and place with honest handling of the unknown-time case.

screens.data: Born: 14 March 1991, 08:42, Austin, Texas (city autocomplete with timezone note 'CST, UTC-6'). Link: 'Not sure of the time? We will show which parts of the chart depend on it.' Button: 'Draw my chart'. Line: 'Calculated on this device. Works offline.'

screens.title: Onboarding: your chart, revealed
screens.purpose: Deliver the first payoff in plain words before a single term goes unexplained.
screens.hero: The bodygraph drawing itself line by line, then three plain-language cards sliding under it.
screens.data: 'You are a Generator, 5/1 profile, emotional authority.' Card 1: 'Generator - your energy works like a battery that recharges by doing work you love.' Card 2: 'Emotional authority - your clarity comes after the wave passes, not in the moment.' Button: 'Explore my chart'. Every underlined term already tappable.

screens.title: First launch: empty people shelf
screens.purpose: The empty state for charts of others, seeding the composite habit without pressure.
screens.hero: One filled chart card (yours) beside dotted-outline card slots under small constellations.

screens.title: The bodygraph, mid-exploration
screens.purpose: The core mechanic: tap any element and it explains itself in plain language, first time, every time.
screens.hero: The full bodygraph with the Sacral center tapped, a plain-words sheet risen to one-third height.
screens.data: Sheet: 'Sacral center - defined (colored in). Your life force is consistent: when something is right, your gut literally responds before your mind. Gates here: 34 (power), 5 (rhythm).' Chips: 'What is a center?', 'What does defined mean?'. Nine centers, defined ones filled gold-on-indigo, open ones outlined.

screens.title: Lesson 2 of 5: strategy
screens.purpose: The learning path that fixes the number-one churn reason: jargon without explanation.
screens.hero: A vertical scroll lesson where each concept is a constellation card that lights as you pass it.
screens.data: 'Lesson 2: To respond, not to chase.' Real-life example: 'You post your portfolio and a client writes back - that pull in your gut is the response Generators run on.' Progress: lessons Type ✓, Strategy (reading), Authority, Profile, Centers. Each lesson '4-6 min'. End check: 'Try it today: notice one thing you responded to versus one you initiated.'

screens.title: Now: today's transits
screens.purpose: The practitioner's daily instrument: which gates the sky activates this hour.

Your activation note: 'Transit Gate 34 completes your channel 34-20 today: extra drive, watch for busyness.' Timeline scrubber shows the next 24 h of gate changes.

screens.title: Gate change notification
screens.purpose: The moment practitioners pay for: the sky shifted and the app taps your shoulder.

screens.data: Push at 15:40: 'Sun moved: Gate 33 → Gate 7. The Army - leadership through listening. Active until 21 Jul, 03:12.' In-app: the 33 star dims, 7 flares, the golden channel line to your Gate 31 draws itself with the caption 'This transit defines your channel 7-31 (leadership).'

Compromise 1: channel 12-22.' Plain line: 'Together you have 7 of 9 centers defined - this connection feels steadier than either of you alone.'

Buttons: 'Unlock for $24', 'Restore purchase'.

astrology-8.territory: The practitioner checks the app at dawn with coffee, not for wonder but for logistics: when today should the transfer go out, when should the difficult call happen. The interface answers with the calm of a morning almanac, warm sandalwood paper and marigold light, a working document that treats the panchanga as a schedule, not a mystery.

palette.note: Saffron-vermillion paints only the favorable windows and the current moment on the day arc, unfavorable stretches are plain unpainted paper, never black, never threatening.

astrology-8.typography: Fraunces for headings and window names, Spectral for the panchanga and body: two warm serifs at different temperatures give it the feel of a well-set almanac page rather than an app.
astrology-8.motif: The sunrise-to-sunrise arc: the Vedic day drawn as one continuous arc across the top of every screen, favorable windows gilded in saffron, the present moment a small climbing sun, so time itself is the interface.

ia.coreObject: The day: one sunrise-to-sunrise arc carrying your personal windows and the panchanga
ia.primaryLoop: Every morning the user reads today's arc, drags one or two real tasks into the gilded windows, and returns because a 15-minute heads-up fires just before each window opens.

screens.title: Onboarding: birth details
screens.purpose: Collect date, exact time, and place once, with honesty about the engine.

astronomy-stargazing-4.territory: It is 4:50 a.m., the truck is packed, and the person wants one fact before driving to the lake: is today worth it. The interface answers like a farmer's almanac left open on the kitchen table, the moon already drawn, the good days already circled in red. No greeting, no feed, no astrology, just the page for today.

palette.note: Cream paper carries everything; ink navy does the reading work, and almanac red appears only as circles around best days and the full-moon date, never as decoration.

astronomy-stargazing-4.typography: Tiempos Headline sets the moon phase and dates like an almanac masthead, National 2 with tabular figures keeps rise and set times aligned to the minute.
astronomy-stargazing-4.motif: A stipple-engraved woodcut moon disc, drawn like a 19th-century lithograph, that waxes and wanes as the single hero of every day page.

ia.coreObject: the day: one calendar day carrying its moon phase, rise and set times, and a task rating
ia.primaryLoop: Open before heading out, read the phase and today's fishing or planting rating in one glance, then plan the weekend from the red-circled days.

astronomy-stargazing-5.territory: It is 23:40 in a dark field, eyes are dark-adapted, the scope is humming, and the owner is done being babysat by a toy app. The interface answers like an observatory console: black, exact, monospaced, every number where a trained hand expects it. It respects night vision and it respects the plan.

palette.note: True black for OLED and dark fields; red is the working accent because it preserves dark adaptation, and in Night Mode the entire interface collapses into shades of that red.

astronomy-stargazing-5.typography: IBM Plex Mono carries every coordinate, timestamp, and frame count like an instrument readout; Inter handles labels and stays out of the way.
astronomy-stargazing-5.motif: The reticle: a hairline crosshair-and-graticule frame that surrounds every target card and rotates slowly while the scope is slewing.

ia.coreObject: the target: an imaging target with coordinates, a capture plan, and its accumulated frames
ia.primaryLoop: Build tonight's queue at dusk, let it run while sleeping, and check the frame counts over coffee the next morning.

screens.title: Onboarding: find the scope

screens.data: This app: go-to by RA/Dec, pre-slew setup, night queue, session log. Seestar app: stacking, live view, firmware updates. Line below: 'Both connect at once. We are the second remote, not a replacement.'

screens.title: Empty night plan

screens.hero: An empty reticle centered on the page, waiting
screens.data: 'No targets queued for tonight.' Primary button: Add target by RA/Dec. Secondary: Pick from recent objects. Footnote: 'Astronomical darkness tonight: 22:51 to 03:34.'

screens.title: Tonight, queue running
screens.purpose: The 02:14 glance from the tent: what is being captured right now and what comes next.
screens.hero: The active target card with a live frame counter inside its reticle
screens.data: 02:14. Now imaging: M27 Dumbbell Nebula, frame 34 of 120, 10s subs, gain 80, LP filter in. Elapsed 41m. Next in queue: NGC 6946, slews at 03:05 (transit 03:22). Queue: 2 of 3 complete. Button: Pause queue.

screens.purpose: Configure framing, filter, and exposure before moving the scope, so it arrives ready.
screens.hero: A framing preview with the reticle showing the sensor footprint over a star field
screens.data: Target: M27. Framing: rotate 12°, offset 0.2° N to include NGC 6853 halo. Filter: LP in. Exposure: 10s × 120 frames. Gain: 80. Estimated run: 24m + dither. Button: Slew configured.

screens.title: Queue builder

astronomy-stargazing-6.territory: The person opens their calendar to plan something that matters to them, a launch, a haircut, a first practice of the cycle, and wants the Moon's quiet counsel right there among the meetings, not in a separate mystical app. The interface answers with the calm of a well-kept paper almanac: unhurried, precise, a little reverent, never glowing or gimmicky. It should feel like the Moon politely joined your week, not like your week got dragged into astrology.

palette.note: The page stays paper-calm all day; midnight-ink indigo is reserved for the moon discs, the terminator hairline and primary actions, and the whole surface cools by a few degrees of warmth after local sunset.

astronomy-stargazing-6.typography: Newsreader carries the morning card and every plain-words explanation like a printed almanac entry, while Inter sets the calendar grid and controls so the ritual voice and the utility never blur.
astronomy-stargazing-6.motif: The terminator: every day cell carries a small moon disc whose lit fraction is astronomically exact, and today's row is crossed by a single hairline marking the light-shadow boundary sweeping through the month.

ia.coreObject: The lunar day, a calendar day annotated with phase, Moon sign and its fitness for what you planned
ia.primaryLoop: Each morning the person reads the day card (phase, sign, one prompt), checks upcoming plans against lunar windows, and returns because the layer lives inside the same calendar their real week lives in.

baby-tracking-2.territory: An exclusively pumping mom lives with a quiet background arithmetic: how much came out today, how much is in the freezer, how long it will last. The interface answers like a well-kept pantry: cool frost-clean surfaces, every bag a real object on a shelf, and the days-left number always on top, so the anxiety of the running total becomes the calm of visible stock. Tender, but never cutesy, because this is inventory that matters.

palette.note: Frost blue-white like the inside of a freezer, with one warm raspberry reserved for milk itself, bag fills, volumes, and the days-left numeral, so the eye always finds the milk first.

baby-tracking-2.typography: Karla for labels and notes, warm and even-tempered, with the days-left forecast set in Fraunces at 56pt so the one number she checks ten times a day has the weight of a headline.
baby-tracking-2.motif: The shelf of bags: the freezer stash is always drawn as rows of small rounded bag shapes sitting on shelf lines, each with its date and volume, and thawing one physically slides it off the shelf.

ia.coreObject: The milk bag (volume, freeze date, storage location) on a shelf, fed by pumping sessions and drained by thaws
ia.primaryLoop: Log each session in five seconds, bag what goes to the freezer, thaw bags as baby needs them, and glance at the days-left forecast to feel ahead of the week.

baby-tracking-3.territory: The night before the four-month checkup, a first-time parent rehearses answers they half remember: how many feeds, how many wet diapers, is that normal. The interface answers with the composure of walking in prepared: warm manila-folder calm, a well-visit form whose checkboxes have quietly filled themselves from two ordinary weeks of logging, and nothing to memorize ever again. Tender at home, credible in the exam room.

palette.note: Manila folder warmth around white form pages, with a ballpoint-pen blue reserved for everything the app fills in on the parent's behalf, so at a glance you can tell what the data answered versus what the form asked.

baby-tracking-3.typography: Public Sans, the U.S. federal forms typeface, for the form and interface, with the parent's own questions rendered in Caveat so what the doctor asks and what you want to ask never blur together.
baby-tracking-3.motif: The checkbox that fills itself: the well-visit question list is always visible somewhere in the app, and each ordinary log entry visibly ticks another box in pen blue, so daily tracking reads as progress toward being ready.

ia.coreObject: The visit sheet, a well-visit question list auto-answered from the running log of feeds, diapers, sleep, and weight

baby-tracking-5.territory: It is 3:12 am, the baby is latched, one arm is pinned, eyes are half shut, and any bright pixel feels like an insult. The interface answers by almost not being there: a truly black screen, three slabs of button in the bottom third where the thumb already rests, and one dim ember of a timer. It asks for nothing, remembers everything, and lets the morning self read what the night self did.

palette.note: True OLED black with warm low-lumen text; the single ember red marks only the running timer and the active side, chosen because dim red light disturbs night vision least, and nothing on screen ever exceeds candle brightness.

baby-tracking-5.typography: Lexend throughout, built for effortless reading, with the timer set as a single 64pt light numeral, so 14:32 is legible through half-open eyes at minimum screen brightness.
baby-tracking-5.motif: The bottom-third triptych: three full-width button slabs stacked in the lowest third of the screen where a one-handed thumb naturally lands, with the upper two-thirds kept as pure black void holding only the ember timer.

ia.coreObject: The feeding session (side or bottle, start, duration, volume) logged in the dark
ia.primaryLoop: Wake, press one of three slabs without looking, feed, press again, sleep; read the assembled night at breakfast and glance at the lock screen all day for the last-feed time.

baby-tracking-6.territory: A parent at work carries half their attention home to the baby; a nanny mid-shift has one free hand and no patience for menus. The interface answers both with quiet certainty: for the caregiver, four soft buttons and nothing else; for the parent, a gentle live thread proving the day is being written down without anyone chasing anyone. Warmth without cuteness, and a night face that whispers.

palette.note: Warm linen and soft browns keep every screen calm at any hour; the muted coral marks only live events arriving, and after 22:00 the whole palette drops to a near-black amber night face with no white flashes.

baby-tracking-6.typography: Nunito Sans throughout, rounded and generous, with event times in a slightly heavier weight; the type feels like a kind handwritten note without resorting to script.
baby-tracking-6.motif: The day card: every shift accumulates into one rounded, stamp-cornered summary card (feeds, naps, diapers, mood, a note) that slides closed at day's end like a page in a baby book, and the archive is a shelf of these cards.

ia.coreObject: The shift entry: a timestamped event (feed, nap, diaper, note with photo) written by one caregiver, readable and commentable by parents, editable only by its author
ia.primaryLoop: The caregiver logs each event with one tap as the day unfolds, the parent watches entries arrive live within seconds and reads the day card at night, and that twice-daily rhythm of write and read is the whole product.

baby-tracking-8.territory: The parents using this left the NICU with a discharge sheet measured in milliliters and a fear measured in grams, and they are running feeds every three hours around the clock. The interface answers with tender exactness: soft and warm like a nursery, but numerically strict like the ward they just left, never rounding, never converting, and whispering instead of glowing at 3 AM.

palette.note: Ward-mint marks on-plan values and completed feeds while deviations render in a soft amber, never red; the 3 AM screen drops everything to near-black with dim warm gray text so the room stays asleep.

baby-tracking-8.typography: ABC Favorit with tabular figures keeps every milliliter and gram reading in strict vertical alignment like a hospital chart; its rounded cut softens the clinical grid into something a exhausted parent can love.
baby-tracking-8.motif: The syringe graduation: every volume control and chart axis is ruled in true 1 ml tick marks like the feeding syringes from the ward, making no-rounding a visible physical promise rather than a settings claim.

ia.coreObject: The feed (exact ml against the 24-hour plan), joined by weigh-ins charted against corrected age
ia.primaryLoop: Log every feed to the milliliter against the discharge plan around the clock, and return weekly for the weight curve and the PDF the neonatologist actually reads.

blood-pressure-log-4.territory: The person is a chronic patient in a diligent morning routine, carrying a quiet distrust of software that has already erased years of their records once. The interface answers with the permanence and gravity of a paper ledger: nothing decorative, nothing that moves, every number large and every year still reachable. It should feel like the one object in their phone that will outlive the phone.

palette.note: Warm paper ground with near-black ink at maximum contrast for older eyes; the deep clinical teal appears only on actions and the current reading, never as decoration.

blood-pressure-log-4.typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible for everything, with readings set in oversized tabular figures (34pt and up); the type does the reassuring, not the graphics, and nothing on screen is smaller than 17pt.
blood-pressure-log-4.motif: The year spine: a permanent vertical rail of year numerals (2014, 2015 … 2026) running down the left edge of every history view, like the tabbed spine of a paper ledger you can grab and flip to any year.

ia.coreObject: The reading (one dated row: systolic/diastolic, pulse, optional weight and note) accumulated into a lifelong ledger
ia.primaryLoop: Twice a day the person takes a cuff measurement, enters it in under fifteen seconds, and glances at the row settling into the same list that holds twelve years of rows, which is exactly why they come back.

blood-pressure-log-5.territory: It is 7 a.m., the cuff just deflated, and a 68-year-old is holding three numbers in short-term memory that the doctor asked for. The interface answers with the calm of a well-ruled paper ledger: nothing moves, nothing sells, every letter is big enough to read without glasses. The feeling is of a document you own, not an app you rent.

palette.note: Warm paper white with near-black ink at maximum contrast; the single clinical teal appears only on the save action and the systolic column header, never as decoration.

blood-pressure-log-5.typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible for every number and label, sized 22pt minimum for body and 44pt for readings; Source Serif 4 only for the note text, so a note reads like handwriting in the margin of a ledger.
blood-pressure-log-5.motif: The triple cell: every reading everywhere in the app is the same ruled three-box row (SYS | DIA | PULSE) with a hairline underline, like a printed ledger line you fill in with a pen.

ia.coreObject: The reading: three numbers, a timestamp, an optional note, and up to three tags, editable forever
ia.primaryLoop: Measure with the cuff, open the app, type three numbers on the keyboard in five seconds, glance at the last few rows, and close; twice a day, every day, because the doctor said so.

blood-pressure-log-8.territory: A 68-year-old at the kitchen table with a cuff on one side and a glucometer on the other, entering numbers a doctor will actually read. The interface answers with clinical calm for older eyes: big honest digits, no rings, no confetti, the quiet authority of a well-kept paper chart.

palette.note: Beyond black there are only two inks, slate-blue (#2F4A6B) for pressure and teal for sugar, used identically in the feed, the charts, and the report so the two measures are never confused.

blood-pressure-log-8.typography: Public Sans with oversized tabular numerals at large optical sizes; the digits are the interface and every word around them stays small and quiet.
blood-pressure-log-8.motif: The spine: a vertical center rule running down every screen with pressure entries hanging to its left and sugar to its right, exactly the two-column paper chart this replaces.

ia.coreObject: The reading: a timestamped number from a real device, tagged with its moment
ia.primaryLoop: Morning cuff reading and post-meal glucose entered in under fifteen seconds each; the feed quietly builds the one report the doctor asks for.

calendars-tasks-10.territory: An adult daughter checking her phone at lunch, three states away from her mother, carrying the low hum of 'did Mom take her pills, whose weekend is it, what do we tell the cardiologist Thursday'. The interface answers with the steadiness of a good charge nurse: orderly daylight grids, large unambiguous confirmations, and the sense that three siblings are looking at the same truthful page. Worry is not removed — it is given a shape and a schedule.

palette.note: Soft blue-gray daylight with a steady mid-blue reserved for confirmations and the on-duty marker; when every dose dot on the timeline is blue, the whole family exhales.

calendars-tasks-10.typography: IBM Plex Sans throughout, set one size larger than typical and never below regular weight; the parent's screens jump to 22pt with full-width buttons, so the same typeface serves both generations.
calendars-tasks-10.motif: The confirmation relay: each scheduled dose is an open circle on a shared timeline that fills solid blue the moment it is confirmed, and it fills simultaneously on every family member's phone.

ia.coreObject: The care day: today's doses, who is on duty, and what is being observed for the next doctor visit

calendars-tasks-2.territory: A professional starts the morning assembling the day in their head from three apps, low-grade anxious that something scheduled and something promised will collide at 2pm. The interface answers with the calm authority of a Swiss railway timetable: one column of truth, daylight white, everything in time order, nothing moved without your hand. Reading the day should feel like exhaling.

palette.note: Pure white page with cool gray station-board surfaces; cobalt is spent only on the now-line and the item currently underway, so blue always means 'this moment'.

calendars-tasks-2.typography: Helvetica Now Display for times and headers, Helvetica Now Text for items; the timetable heritage is literal, with big tabular times flush left like a departures board.
calendars-tasks-2.motif: The spine: a single vertical rule running the full height of every day, with events docked as solid blocks, tasks as ticketed stubs, and habits as small punched circles, all hanging off the same line.

ia.coreObject: The day: one chronological feed where calendar events, deadline tasks, and habits hold positions on a shared spine

calendars-tasks-4.territory: She walks out of a night shift at 7:40am with a fried brain and one question: when am I on next and what will this month actually pay. The interface answers with cool, pre-computed daylight order: nothing to type, the pattern already stamped, the money already done. It should feel like the one part of her schedule that never needs explaining.

palette.note: Day shifts sit flat in cool slate; only night shifts and pay figures earn the marigold, so the moon and the money always pop first.

calendars-tasks-4.typography: IBM Plex Sans for labels with IBM Plex Mono tabular figures for hours and pay, so the whole app reads like a well-kept duty roster.
calendars-tasks-4.motif: The rotation stamp: your 2/2 pattern is a small inked block (D D N N — —) that visibly stamps itself across the month when applied, and doubles as the app's signature mark.
