meditation-mindfulness-1.territory: It is dusk after a long day and the person does not want to browse, they want to be led by the one voice they have chosen to trust. The interface answers like a pilgrimage trail at nightfall: one path, one next step, everything else in shadow. The feeling is devotion without decoration, a student's relief at not having to choose.

palette.note: A warm plum dusk rather than a cold black; the single terracotta ember marks only the current stage on the path and the play button, so the eye always knows where today lives.

meditation-mindfulness-1.typography: Freight Text for every word the teacher speaks or writes, set generously like a printed retreat handbook, with GT America in small caps for wayfinding labels only.
meditation-mindfulness-1.motif: The stone path: all 80 stages rendered as a single winding line of stepping stones ascending the screen, walked stones warm-toned, the current one glowing ember, everything ahead unlit and unnamed.

ia.coreObject: The stage: one session on the 80-stage path, with the teacher's spoken context and the student's note
ia.primaryLoop: Sit once a day: two minutes of the teacher framing today's stage, the practice itself, one written line after; the pull back is the next unlit stone and the relationship with the one voice.

screens.title: Onboarding: meet the teacher
screens.purpose: Establish the entire premise, one human with a lineage, before any feature talk.
screens.hero: A full-bleed portrait photograph in warm dusk light with a 40-second audio greeting waveform.
screens.data: 'This is Tenzin Dorje. 26 years of practice in the Kagyu tradition, teaching since 2009.' Play chip: 'Hear Tenzin explain the path, 0:40.' One line in his voice as pull-quote: 'You will not browse here. We will walk, one sitting at a time.' Button: 'Walk with Tenzin'.

screens.title: Onboarding: choose your sitting time
screens.purpose: Anchor the daily ritual to a real moment in the student's day, gently.
screens.hero: A dusk-to-night gradient dial with three warm presets and one custom slot.
screens.data: 'When will you sit?' Presets: 'With morning coffee 7:00', 'Lunch pause 13:00', 'Before bed 22:00' (selected). Note: 'Miss a day and the path simply waits. Nothing is lost, nothing resets.' Button: 'Begin stage one'.

screens.title: First launch: the path at stone one
screens.purpose: The empty state as a vista: eighty stones visible, only the first one lit.
screens.hero: The stone path receding upward into dusk, stone 1 glowing ember, stones 2-80 as dim unnamed shapes.
screens.data: Stone 1: 'Arriving - 12 min'. Overlay line: 'Eighty stages. One order. The next stone lights when this one is walked.' Button: 'Sit for stage 1'. No search bar, no categories, no library link anywhere.

screens.title: The path, stage 23
screens.purpose: The daily home mid-journey: where you stand, where you have been, one step visible ahead.
screens.hero: The path scrolled to stone 23 glowing ember, 22 warm walked stones below, stone 24 barely outlined.
screens.data: Stone 23: 'Resting in open awareness - 18 min'. Walked trail shows small date marks: 'stone 22 · yesterday', 'stone 21 · Jul 8'. Header: '23 of 80 · walking since 14 Jun'. Button: 'Sit today'. Tapping any walked stone reopens that session freely.

screens.title: Before the practice: the teacher's framing
screens.purpose: The 2-3 minute context segment that separates a path from a track list.
screens.hero: The teacher's portrait dimmed to near-silhouette with a spoken-word transcript scrolling in Freight Text.
screens.data: 'Stage 23, before we sit - 2:40.' Transcript excerpt: 'Last week you held attention on the breath. Today we loosen that grip. Notice what remains aware when you stop directing.' Buttons: 'Continue to practice' appears only when the audio ends, 'Read instead' for transcript-only.

screens.title: In the sitting
screens.purpose: The practice screen itself: almost nothing, held by warmth.
screens.hero: A near-black plum screen with a single ember dot that dims over the session's length, no timer digits by default.
screens.data: Stage 23 · 18 min · Tenzin's voice. Controls appear on tap: pause, back 15 s, 'show remaining time' toggle (off by default). End bell: one strike, then 20 s of silence before the journal prompt.

screens.title: After: one line in the journal
screens.purpose: Close each stage with a single written observation, building the student's own record.
screens.hero: One warm input line under the just-walked stone, keyboard already open.
screens.data: Prompt in Tenzin's phrasing: 'What did you notice when you stopped directing?' Entry: 'kept grabbing the breath again, three times, then something settled.' Below: journal stream, 'stage 22 - fell asleep at the end, oddly fine with it', 'stage 21 - restless, sat anyway.' Button: 'Seal stage 23' - lights stone 24.

screens.title: The locked stone ahead
screens.purpose: Handle the skip attempt with the product's own philosophy instead of a paywall reflex.
screens.hero: Stone 31 tapped: it stays unlit, a short letterpress card from the teacher rises.
screens.data: 'Stage 31 is seven sittings ahead.' Teacher's note: 'The order is the teaching. What stage 31 asks of you is built in 24 through 30. I would rather you arrive ready.' Single button: 'Return to stage 23'. No 'unlock now' option exists at any price.

screens.title: Returning after nine days away
screens.purpose: The lapse state: welcome back without shame mechanics, path exactly where it was left.
screens.hero: The path unchanged, stone 24 still glowing, a short handwritten-style note from the teacher pinned above it.
screens.data: 'You sat last on Jul 1. The path kept your place.' Teacher audio, 1:10: 'Nine days is not failure, it is material. Sit today and notice what the gap felt like.' Button: 'Sit for stage 24'. No streak counter anywhere in the app, before or after the gap.

screens.title: Monthly live sitting
screens.purpose: The living-relationship mechanic: real question time with the actual teacher.
screens.hero: A candle-lit live room card with the question queue rendered as folded paper slips.
screens.data: 'Live with Tenzin - Sunday Jul 26, 19:00 CET · 312 students registered.' Your slip: 'Stage 23: is drowsiness a problem or a message?' Queue shows 41 questions, teacher answers by theme. Replay of Jun 28 session (1:04:12) available below with chapter marks.

screens.title: The year on the path
screens.purpose: The paywall as a commitment ceremony, in the teacher's own voice, after stage 5 is free.
screens.hero: The full 80-stone path seen from above for the first time, the whole route visible, price set like an inscription at the trailhead.
screens.data: 'The full path - $79 a year.' Free: stages 1-5, complete. Included: all 80 stages in order, every framing talk, monthly live sittings, your journal exportable always. Teacher's line: 'This is a year of walking together. If it is not, cancel and keep your journal.' Buttons: 'Join the path, $79/yr', 'Restore purchase'. Footnote: 'A share of every membership goes directly to Tenzin.'

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: The few controls a single-path app honestly needs.
screens.hero: A short list on plum, led by the sitting-time row with its dusk dial.
screens.data: Sitting reminder: 22:00 daily, gentle bell. Downloads: keep next 3 stages offline (on). Bell at session end: single strike / none. Transcripts: on. Export journal (plain text). Live session calendar sync. Restore purchase. Delete account and journal. Version 1.3.

meditation-mindfulness-10.territory: The person arriving here is braced: pain is loud, past apps made it louder by marching attention straight into the hurting place, and trust is at zero. The interface answers with enormous dusk-quiet emptiness and a standing promise of distance, attention always offered an external horizon to rest on, never a body part, so that opening the app already feels like stepping back from the pain rather than toward it.

palette.note: A dusk that is warm rather than cold; the single ember tone lives almost exclusively in the horizon line and never flashes, pulses fast, or demands.

meditation-mindfulness-10.typography: Tiempos Text at generous sizes for instructions and Söhne for the sparse UI, set large and airy because a person at pain level 7 should never have to squint or hunt.
meditation-mindfulness-10.motif: The horizon: one thin luminous line across the dark that rises and falls with the breath, the app's permanent external anchor, present on every screen as the place attention can safely land.

ia.coreObject: The practice session, always paired with its log entry: what was practiced, at what pain level, and what helped
ia.primaryLoop: A short daily practice at a safe distance from the pain plus a thirty-second log, with the flare-up protocol standing by on a widget for the bad moments, and the doctor-ready log giving the whole effort a visible point.

screens.title: Onboarding — Where you are with pain
screens.purpose: Learn the shape of the person's pain without a body diagram or any request to focus on it, setting the tone of distance immediately.
screens.hero: Plain text questions over the resting horizon line, no body illustration anywhere
screens.data: 'How long has pain been part of your life?' → over 3 years · 'Have body scans ever made it worse?' → yes · 'We will never point your attention at the place that hurts. Every practice starts at a distance and you set how close it ever gets.'

screens.title: Onboarding — Your safe anchors
screens.purpose: Choose the external and neutral anchors all practices will use, so the first session is already built from safe material.
screens.hero: Anchor cards floating above the horizon: sound, hands, the room, the breath at the nostrils
screens.data: Chosen anchors: ambient sound ✓, palms resting ✓ · Declined: breath in the chest ('too close to the pain') · Flare protocol installed to home-screen widget · First practice ready: 8 minutes, attention on the room

screens.title: First launch — Starting at a distance
screens.purpose: An empty state that promises smallness and safety instead of a program's ambition.
screens.hero: The horizon line alone in a vast dark field with one soft session card
screens.data: 'Nothing to catch up on. One practice, 8 minutes, attention on sound only — nowhere near the pain. That's the whole day.' · Course ahead: 21 sessions, each unlocked by doing, not by dates · Button: Begin at a distance

screens.title: Today — mid-course, day 6
screens.purpose: The daily anchor: today's practice, your position on the course, and last night's flare acknowledged without drama.
screens.hero: Today's session card resting on the horizon, course position as small waypoints along the line
screens.data: Day 6 of 21 · 'Edges, briefly' — 12 min · 'Three visits to the edge of the sensation, three returns to sound. You control every step back.' · Last night: flare logged 7/10, protocol used, sleep block after · This week: 4 practices, 1 flare

screens.title: Practice player — mid-session
screens.purpose: Almost no UI while practicing: the breathing horizon, the voice, and one always-available retreat.
screens.hero: The horizon line rising and falling with the guided breath, everything else faded to near-black
screens.data: 'Edges, briefly' · 4:32 remaining · Voice: '...and step back to the sound of the room. You never have to stay.' · One visible control: 'Step back' — instantly returns the guidance to the neutral anchor · Pause by touching anywhere

screens.title: Flare-up protocol — launched from the widget
screens.purpose: The five-minute emergency practice for when pain takes over, reachable in one motion with zero navigation.
screens.hero: A single full-screen ember-warm horizon breathing slowly, oversized type
screens.data: Flare protocol · 5:00 · Voice and breath only: 'You don't have to fight this wave. Eyes anywhere but inward...' · Started from lock-screen widget at 2:17 am · After: one tap logs it — intensity 8/10, no typing needed at 2 am

screens.title: Log — the thirty-second entry
screens.purpose: Capture intensity, trigger, and what helped while it's fresh, with taps not typing.
screens.hero: Three tap-rows over the resting horizon: how strong, what set it off, what helped
screens.data: Jul 10 · Intensity: 6/10 · Trigger: long drive ✓ (recent: sitting, weather, poor sleep) · What helped: flare protocol ✓ heat pad ✓ · Practice today: 'Edges, briefly' 12 min completed · Streak language absent by design — a hard day is data, not failure

screens.title: Doctor export — the log becomes a document
screens.purpose: Compile flares and practices into a clean PDF that makes the next appointment better, the feature that justifies the whole habit.
screens.hero: A white clinical PDF preview standing out against the dusk interface
screens.data: Report: Jun 10 – Jul 10 · 5 flares (avg 6.8/10, 3 at night) · Common trigger: prolonged sitting (4 of 5) · 24 practices, 262 min total · Flare protocol used 5×, rated helpful 4× · Export PDF / print · 'Bring it to your pain specialist — it reads in under a minute.'

screens.title: Night block — falling asleep with pain
screens.purpose: The dedicated sleep practice for pain that won't quiet down, built on coexistence rather than fighting.
screens.hero: The horizon dimmed to its faintest, screen at minimum brightness, timer optional
screens.data: 'Sleeping alongside it' · 20 min, voice fades out after 12 · 'The goal isn't to make it stop. It's to let sleep arrive anyway.' · Screen dims to black after 60 seconds · Used 8 nights this month, most-played practice in the library

screens.title: Anchor library — the body-scan replacement
screens.purpose: The practice shelf for days when turning inward is not an option, every practice labeled by its distance from the body.
screens.hero: Practice cards arranged by distance, farthest from the body first
screens.data: External: 'The room around you' 6 min · 'Sound only' 10 min · Neutral body: 'Palms and weight' 8 min · Approach work: 'Edges, briefly' 12 min (course day 6+) · Every card labeled: 'no body attention' / 'neutral zones only' / 'approaches the edge — you steer'

screens.title: Paywall — end of the first week
screens.purpose: A quiet ask framed against what pain already costs, after the free week proved the method fits this body.
screens.hero: A single price card resting under the horizon, no countdown, no crossed-out prices
screens.data: Week one is free and stays yours: the flare protocol and your log never lock · Full course, night block, and anchor library: $11/month or $70/year · 'Less than one physical therapy copay a month.' · Cancel anytime, log exports free forever · Restore purchase

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: Control over voice, warnings, and data with the same non-negotiable gentleness.
screens.hero: A short dark list, generous type, nothing buried
screens.data: Voice: Anna (calm, slow) / Michael · Body-scan content: hidden entirely ✓ (default) · Notifications: practice reminder 8 pm, no motivational language ever · Widget: flare protocol ✓ · Export full log (PDF/CSV) · Delete all data · Restore purchase

meditation-mindfulness-3.territory: It is 3:07 AM, the mind is sprinting, the alarm is four hours away, and any light or choice is an enemy. The interface answers with near-total absence: a black room with one warm handle to hold, everything already decided during daylight. Dark is not an aesthetic here, it is the product working. Daytime screens are a separate, softly lit dusk world where all the choosing happens.

palette.note: True black at night with text dimmed well below normal contrast standards on purpose, moonlight lavender kept to one button and one thread of light, while daytime screens warm the same palette toward a dusk gradient #1C1830 to #2E2440.

meditation-mindfulness-3.typography: Canela Light for the few words that appear at night, spoken-voice soft at large sizes, with Untitled Sans for daytime settings and logs, and nothing bold anywhere after dark.
meditation-mindfulness-3.motif: The resume thread: a single thin line of lavender light representing the story, with a small glowing break at the exact minute you fell asleep, and pressing the one button makes the thread continue from the break.

ia.coreObject: The night session (the recording, the minute you drifted off, and the wake-up it answered)
ia.primaryLoop: At the 3 AM wake-up the user opens straight into a black screen with one button and the story resumes where sleep took them, and each morning a two-tap check-in narrows the lineup to what provably works.

screens.title: When do you wake?
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 1: set the night window that flips the whole app into its 3 AM form.
screens.hero: A dial on a dusk gradient marking the usual wake-window against the sleep hours.
screens.data: My night wakings usually happen: 2:30 to 4:00 AM. Alarm: 7:00 AM. Statement: inside this window the app opens black, silent, and choiceless. Nothing to configure at night, that is the point.

screens.title: Choose your lineup while it's light out
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 2: pick the two or three formats that will be waiting at 3 AM.
screens.hero: Three large format cards on the dusk gradient, each with a 20-second preview.
screens.data: Formats: a monotone story (Marram Grass, read at 55 words a minute), a hypnotic session (Heavy Coat, 24 min), a wordless breathing anchor (Four Six, no voice). Pick 2 or 3. Line: at night you will never see a catalog, only these.

screens.title: Nothing queued yet
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state, deliberately a daytime screen.
screens.hero: An unlit resume thread across the dusk screen with the lineup slots empty beside it.
screens.data: Headline: Your night lineup is empty. Sub: choose two or three formats now, while choosing is easy. If tonight comes first: one default monotone story stands in, marked as the stand-in until you pick.

screens.title: 3:07 AM
screens.purpose: Main screen mid-use: the night mode doing its only job.
screens.hero: A black screen, the resume thread with its glowing break, and one large soft button. Nothing else.
screens.data: Text, dim and large: Marram Grass, you drifted at 14:32. Button: Continue. Volume already at your night level, 35%. No navigation, no clock counting down, brightness pinned to minimum.

screens.title: The thread continues
screens.purpose: The signature resume mechanic at its earning-its-keep moment.
screens.hero: The thread's break sealing shut as playback resumes a beat before the drift point.
screens.data: Resuming Marram Grass at 14:10, 22 seconds before where you faded, voice slowed 8% for the night. If pressed again within a minute: switches to the breathing anchor without asking. Sleep detection: no motion plus no screen touch for 6 min marks the new drift point.

screens.title: Morning, two taps
screens.purpose: The daylight check-in that trains the lineup.
screens.hero: One question on the dusk gradient with two large answers.
screens.data: Last night, 3:07 AM waking, Marram Grass: did you get back to sleep? Back under in a while / Stayed awake. Optional third tap: how long it felt, under 20 min or longer. Effect shown plainly: Marram Grass is now 7 for 9 on your 3 AM wakings.

screens.title: Your lineup, ranked by your nights
screens.purpose: The narrowing mechanic: proof replacing choice.
screens.hero: The two or three format cards reordered by their real success rate, each with its record printed like a quiet scoreboard.
screens.data: Marram Grass: 7 of 9 nights back to sleep. Four Six breathing: 5 of 7. Heavy Coat: 2 of 6, suggestion offered once: swap it for this week's new hypnotic session? One tap keeps or swaps, never at night.

screens.title: New this week
screens.purpose: The weekly drop that answers worn-thin libraries.
screens.hero: A daytime shelf with three fresh recordings, this week's date pressed into the header like a postmark.
screens.data: Week of Oct 12: Inventory of a Hardware Store (monotone, 41 min), Slack Tide (hypnotic, 26 min), a re-recording of Four Six with a lower voice. Favorites never leave: your saved 6 recordings, kept permanently. Next drop: Sunday.

screens.title: Your nights, on paper
screens.purpose: The wake-up log for the doctor conversation.
screens.hero: A 30-night dot chart, one row per night, wakings as small marks with back-to-sleep marks in lavender.
screens.data: Last 30 nights: 22 had a waking, median waking 3:10 AM, back under within about 20 min on 16 of them. 90-day trend: wakings unchanged, time-to-return shortening. Export PDF for your doctor. Footer: built only from your morning check-ins, no microphone, no camera, ever.

screens.title: For the nights that count
screens.purpose: Paywall, tone-matched, shown only in daylight hours by rule.
screens.hero: A single dusk-gradient card with the resume thread running through it, no urgency, no timer.
screens.data: Free: one story, night mode, morning check-ins. Full: $69.99 per year or $10.99 monthly, the weekly new recordings, all three formats, the doctor log export. Line printed on the card: this screen never appears between 9 PM and 9 AM. Buttons: Continue, Restore purchase.

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: The night window, the guarantees, and the volume that never surprises.
screens.hero: A short daytime list headed by the night-window dial.
screens.data: Night window: 2:30 to 4:00 AM. Night volume: 35%, locked against system changes. Notifications: none at night, guaranteed, including rating prompts, a line stating the app has never once asked for a rating at night. Playback: voice slowdown 8%. Delete my log.

meditation-mindfulness-4.territory: An engineer who has dismissed meditation for years is giving it one skeptical try, arms crossed, waiting for the first whiff of chakras to close the app. The interface answers like a good methods section: cited, precise, unembarrassed by its own rigor. The feeling is of being taken seriously by a tool that shows its work.

palette.note: The white of a journal reprint with ink-dark text; the single indigo behaves like a citation link and a data series color, marking mechanisms, references and your own plotted measurements, never mood.

meditation-mindfulness-4.typography: Charter for mechanism explanations and reference entries, carrying the credibility of academic print, with Inter for interface labels and IBM Plex Mono for every self-assessment number.
meditation-mindfulness-4.motif: The paired dots: every practice is bracketed by two small measurement dots (before and after) joined by a vertical delta line, and months of these pairs accumulate into the app's signature chart.

ia.coreObject: The measured session: a practice bracketed by a 30-second before/after self-assessment, preceded by its mechanism
ia.primaryLoop: Rate the state, read two minutes of mechanism, sit, rate again; the return pull is the slowly accumulating chart of paired dots that answers 'is this actually doing anything' with the user's own data.

screens.title: Onboarding: baseline in 30 seconds
screens.purpose: Open with measurement, not promises, so the skeptic's first act is generating their own control data.
screens.hero: Three horizontal 0-10 scales with draggable dots on a white sheet, mono digits updating live.
screens.data: 'Before anything else, a baseline.' Anxiety today: 6. Sleep quality this week: 4. Sustained focus: 5. Footnote: 'Self-report scales, the same instrument used in most cited studies. You will re-measure after each practice.' Button: 'Save baseline'.

screens.title: Onboarding: pick a voice, not a guru
screens.purpose: Make the guide explicitly interchangeable, the anti-charisma stance as a feature.
screens.hero: Three equal audio cards with 15-second sample waveforms, no photos, no bios.
screens.data: Voices: 'Sarah - measured, slower pace', 'David - neutral, minimal', 'Text only - no narration, on-screen instructions.' Sample line each: 'Attention drifts. Noticing the drift is the repetition that trains the network.' Note: 'Switch anytime in Settings. The method is the product, not the person.' Button: 'Start Level 1'.

screens.title: First launch: Level 1 open
screens.purpose: The empty state as a syllabus: ten levels visible, scope honest, first session sized small.
screens.hero: A numbered syllabus column, Level 1 expanded, levels 2-10 titled but folded.
screens.data: 'Level 1: Attention as a trainable variable - 6 sessions, 8-12 min each.' Folded: 'Level 2: The breath as a control knob', 'Level 3: Working with thoughts'... 'Level 10: Open monitoring.' Line: 'No session is locked by time. Finish a level's checkpoint to open the next.' Button: 'Session 1.1 - 8 min'.

screens.title: The mechanism, before session 2.3
screens.purpose: The core differentiator: two minutes on why this works, with the citation in the footer.
screens.hero: A Charter-set explainer page with one inline diagram of the exhale-heart rate loop, styled like a journal figure.
screens.data: 'Why a slow exhale calms you: exhaling activates the vagus nerve, which slows heart rate directly. Extending the exhale beyond the inhale tips the balance toward the parasympathetic state. Effect onset: under 2 minutes.' Figure 1: breath curve vs heart rate trace. Footer citation: 'Zaccaro et al., 2018, Front Hum Neurosci - How breath-control can change your life. Effect size: moderate.' Button: 'Begin practice, 10 min'.

screens.title: Mid-practice
screens.purpose: The sitting screen for people who distrust ambience: quiet, literal, instrument-like.
screens.hero: A single thin exhale-pacing line breathing across white, elapsed time in small mono digits, nothing else.
screens.data: Session 2.3: exhale-extended breathing, 4 s in / 8 s out. Pacer line expands and contracts on the cycle. 06:12 / 10:00 in the corner (visible by default, this audience wants the number). Voice line sample: 'If you are counting heartbeats, stop. Just follow the line.'

screens.title: After: the second dot
screens.purpose: Close the measurement bracket while the state is fresh, in under 30 seconds.
screens.hero: The same three scales, pre-practice dots ghosted in place, post dots being set, deltas computing live.
screens.data: Anxiety: 6 → 4 (-2). Focus: 5 → 6 (+1). Sleep: '(rated weekly, next prompt Sunday)'. Mono summary line: 'Session 2.3 pair saved · 41st measured session.' Note: 'No-change and negative deltas are data too. Skip honestly rather than guess.' Button: 'Save pair'.

screens.title: My data: three months of pairs
screens.purpose: The retention engine: the user's own longitudinal evidence, plotted without spin.
screens.hero: The signature paired-dots chart: 90 days of before/after pairs with a trend line through the deltas.
screens.data: Anxiety series: baseline 6.1 avg (April) → 4.7 avg (July), 62 measured sessions. Median within-session delta: -1.3. Callout on Jun 14: 'pair 7→7, no change, tagged: slept 4 h.' Toggle: Anxiety / Focus / Sleep. Sober footnote: 'Self-report trends, not a clinical measure. Export CSV to inspect the raw pairs.'

screens.title: Level 2 checkpoint
screens.purpose: The gate between levels: a practice with no pacing aids plus a written self-assessment.
screens.hero: An exam-sheet card, checkbox criteria on the left, one unaided 12-minute practice slot on the right.
screens.data: 'Checkpoint: hold exhale-extended breathing for 12 minutes without the pacer.' Post-assessment: 'Rate your ability to notice drift within a few breaths: 7/10.' Result: 'Level 2 complete - 6 sessions, avg anxiety delta -1.6. Level 3: Working with thoughts, now open.' Retake allowed, attempts logged.

screens.title: Reference: technique entries
screens.purpose: The honest encyclopedia: each technique with mechanism, evidence grade and effect size, including weak ones.
screens.hero: An A-Z reference list in Charter, each entry carrying an evidence badge like a journal tag.
screens.data: 'Exhale-extended breathing - evidence: strong (12 RCTs), effect on state anxiety: moderate.' 'Body scan - evidence: moderate, effect on sleep onset: small-to-moderate.' 'Visualization - evidence: limited, listed for completeness; we do not teach it in the course.' Each entry links its 2-4 key studies with year and journal.

screens.title: Library: any session in two taps
screens.purpose: Fix the named gap from Healthy Minds reviews: past sessions findable and repeatable instantly.
screens.hero: A flat chronological session list with a persistent filter row, search field on top.
screens.data: Filters: Level (1-10), technique, duration. Search 'exhale' → 'Session 2.3 - Exhale-extended breathing, 10 min, practiced 14 times, median delta -1.5.' Row action: 'Repeat now'. Pinned: 'Your most repeated: 2.3 (14×), 1.4 (9×)'.

screens.title: Subscription, stated like a methods section
screens.purpose: The paywall for skeptics: exact scope, exact price, user's own data as the only argument.
screens.hero: A plain white card with the user's own delta chart thumbnail above the price, no testimonials, no countdown.
screens.data: 'Your 14 free sessions: median anxiety delta -1.4.' Full course: $50/year. Included: all 10 levels and checkpoints, the reference with citations, unlimited history and CSV export. Free tier keeps: Level 1 and all your recorded data forever. Buttons: 'Subscribe $50/yr', 'Restore purchase'. Footnote: 'Team licenses for engineering orgs: 10+ seats, contact us.'

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: Instrument calibration: voice, scales, data ownership.
screens.hero: A grouped list led by the voice selector with the three sample cards inline.
screens.data: Voice: Sarah / David / Text only (set: David). Assessment scales: 3 default, add 'Irritability' (custom, 0-10). Weekly sleep prompt: Sunday 09:00. Pacer visibility: on. Citations: show inline / footer only. Export all data (CSV). Delete all data. Restore purchase. Version 1.9.

meditation-mindfulness-5.territory: The therapist opens it in the seven minutes between sessions, tired of asking 'did you try the exercise?' from memory. The interface answers with dusk-toned stillness and almost no chrome: one glance shows who practiced and who is struggling, without a single alarm-red badge. It carries the same calm the therapist is trying to teach.

palette.note: A pale rose-into-violet dusk gradient marks only the arc from last session to next; completions are quiet ink dots, and nothing on the caseload is ever red.

meditation-mindfulness-5.typography: Signifier for client names and report headings, Söhne for the working UI: serious enough for clinical records, soft enough for the subject matter.
meditation-mindfulness-5.motif: The session arc: a thin dusk-gradient curve stretching from last session to the next, with a small ink dot set on it for every practice the client completes between the two.

meditation-mindfulness-6.territory: The user is inside the first months of a loss, awake at 3:17am or dressing for a funeral, unable to let go and insulted by apps that ask them to. The interface answers with dusk: enormous empty space, a single low horizon of light, almost no UI, and language that names the pain without flinching or cheering. It never measures progress, because grief is not a course.

palette.note: There is no accent color in the UI sense; the dawn-rose light lives only in the horizon line, which sits lower and dimmer on harder screens and never brightens as a reward.

meditation-mindfulness-6.typography: Lora for every word, set large with generous leading and no bold anywhere; the single warm serif voice is the interface, because a second typeface would feel like a second person in the room.
meditation-mindfulness-6.motif: The low horizon: one soft band of dawn-rose light across the bottom of every screen, breathing at the pace of the practice audio, the only moving thing in the interface.

ia.coreObject: The moment (a named hard occasion with its own practice: the first night, the funeral, the anniversary)
ia.primaryLoop: Return when a moment arrives or a wave hits, press the one large word on screen, and be spoken to honestly for a few minutes; the night block catches the 3am wakings

meditation-mindfulness-7.territory: The user sits down with a blood pressure cuff on the table, not a candle: they want their numbers back and they are willing to train for it. The interface answers with dusk-quiet discipline, a near-dark room where one luminous breathing line does the coaching and the numbers do the motivating, a gym that whispers.

palette.note: The single breath-teal draws the tide line and every measured improvement, everything else sits in warm graphite, and during sessions the whole screen dims to near-black so the line alone remains.

meditation-mindfulness-7.typography: Neue Montreal for headings and coaching copy, IBM Plex Mono for every measured number: the mono digits make breath-holds and blood pressure readings feel like lab data worth trusting week over week.
meditation-mindfulness-7.motif: The tide line: one horizontal luminous wave that paces your breathing in session and then, at rest, becomes the months-long progress chart, the same line doing both jobs.

ia.coreObject: The training block: a paced breathing session inside a 12-week plan, bracketed by measurements
ia.primaryLoop: The user runs one 10-minute paced session a day, logs a cuff reading a few times a week, and returns because the Sunday breath-hold test moves a number they can see.

mind-mapping-1.territory: Someone deep in spatial thought who has been burned before, opening the map on a second device with a flicker of dread. The interface answers with airy-canvas confidence: proof of saving is drawn into the picture itself, so the person can think freely because they can see, at all times, that the work is already safe.

palette.note: The canvas stays near-white and cool so node colors read as the user's own thinking; green is the single status color and it means exactly one thing, written to disk.

mind-mapping-1.typography: GT Walsheim for node text and UI gives the canvas its playful precision, while JetBrains Mono stamps version timestamps and session ticks with archival exactness.
mind-mapping-1.motif: The session rail: a thin timeline along the bottom of the canvas where every editing session leaves a permanent tick, so the proof of save is part of the map itself.

ia.coreObject: The map file: an ordinary document in iCloud Drive carrying its own local session history
ia.primaryLoop: Open a map, think in nodes, close it and watch the session tick get written to the rail, then pick the same map up on any other device without dread.

mind-mapping-2.territory: The user is mid-thought with hands on a Magic Keyboard, terrified of losing the thread while hunting for a menu. The interface answers with an airy, almost silent canvas where the caret is the only thing that moves fast, and every structural change lands with playful, mechanical precision. It should feel like an outliner that learned to breathe in two dimensions.

palette.note: Indigo appears only on the focused node and the active keycap hint, so color always tells you exactly where the keyboard is.

mind-mapping-2.typography: Söhne for node text and UI, Söhne Mono for every keycap badge and shortcut hint; the mono keycaps are the personality, worn like jewelry on an otherwise quiet grotesque.
mind-mapping-2.motif: The keycap badge: a small rounded-square mono glyph (Tab, ⏎, ⌘→) that sits beside whatever it can act on, so the map itself is the shortcut cheat sheet.

ia.coreObject: The map (a tree of nodes with one focused node at all times)
ia.primaryLoop: Open a map, land on the last focused node, and grow or restructure the tree entirely from the keys, returning because capture here is faster than anywhere else

mind-mapping-4.territory: The user finished thinking an hour ago; now they are due in front of a professor or a team and the map has to become a document without betraying them at the last step. The interface answers with the confidence of a print shop that never misses a deadline: an airy canvas for the thinking, and a visible, physical promise that what leaves the app is exactly what is on screen. Playful while you think, exact when you ship.

palette.note: A near-white canvas with a faint dot grid keeps nodes weightless; the violet accent belongs to structure (branch spines, fold lines, page numbers) so color always explains how the map will become pages.

mind-mapping-4.typography: Space Grotesk gives node labels and headers their slightly technical playfulness while Inter keeps outlines and export dialogs plainly legible, thinking type versus shipping type.
mind-mapping-4.motif: The fold line: dashed violet page-break lines that drape over the live canvas showing exactly where the PDF will paginate, turning the map visibly into numbered pages before a single export.

ia.coreObject: The map that ships: a node canvas permanently paired with its outgoing forms (PDF, slides, Markdown)
ia.primaryLoop: Grow the map during study or planning sessions, glance at the fold lines to see how it will paginate, and export the exact artifact the deadline needs, on the device, even on a plane.

mind-mapping-5.territory: An iPad-first founder sits down in a meeting with the Pencil in hand, half-expecting the good features to be locked behind a browser somewhere, because that is what the last two tools did after taking their money. The interface answers with an open canvas and everything present on first launch: airy, immediate, and quietly proud that there is nothing to redirect to.

palette.note: The canvas stays pure white with a whisper of dot grid, iris violet appears only on the selected branch so focus is a color, not a border.

mind-mapping-5.typography: National 2 for the interface set small and quiet, while your own Pencil handwriting is allowed to stay visible inside nodes, so the loudest voice on the canvas is the user's.
mind-mapping-5.motif: The ink branch: connectors are tapered pencil strokes that thicken toward the root, so a finished map reads like something that grew from your hand rather than a diagram tool.

ia.coreObject: The map, a fully local document that never waits on a server or a web version
ia.primaryLoop: Open the canvas in every meeting and thinking session, branch with the Pencil as fast as thoughts arrive, and leave with a map worth presenting, which is why the iPad comes to the meeting at all.

mind-mapping-8.territory: Your head holds forty open loops and every to-do list you have tried collapsed into an unread scroll of guilt. The interface answers with one airy canvas where your whole life stays visible at once: nothing hides below the fold, capture costs one gesture, and finished things settle into calm color instead of disappearing.

palette.note: A near-white sky where each life branch keeps its own soft ink; completed branches cool toward sage while live tasks hold the cobalt, so calm is literally a color you earn.

mind-mapping-8.typography: Space Grotesk gives branch names their playful-precise geometry while Inter keeps task nodes instantly scannable at small sizes, and due dates sit in tabular figures so nothing jitters.
mind-mapping-8.motif: The ripening branch: every branch visibly cools from cobalt to sage as its tasks complete, so progress reads as weather across the map without opening anything.

ia.coreObject: The task node: a checkbox with a due date and reminder living on a branch of one personal life map
ia.primaryLoop: Flick stray thoughts into the inbox all day, sort them onto branches when ready, and glance at the whole map each morning to see what today actually is.

music-streaming-2.territory: The collector has spent years ripping, tagging, and shelving a lossless library on a NAS, and what they feel toward player apps is earned distrust: something always breaks in the car or away from home. The interface answers like a serious piece of audio hardware: matte black faceplate calm, album art as the only light source, and the signal path from your storage to your ears drawn on screen so you can see exactly why it will not fail. Dark because a listening room is dark.

palette.note: Matte hardware black where album art provides the color and glow, with a single standby-LED blue reserved for live signal, the active source, the playing track, and a completed cache, exactly like the power light on an amplifier.

music-streaming-2.typography: Neue Haas Unica for titles and labels in the restrained voice of an amplifier faceplate, with Space Mono for format badges so FLAC 24/96 and 213.8 GB read as engineering facts.
music-streaming-2.motif: The signal chain: a thin horizontal path of nodes, source to phone to output, always drawn on the now-playing screen with the live segments lit LED blue, so where your music is coming from is never a mystery.

ia.coreObject: The track file (format, bit depth, source, cache state) inside an album, streamed directly from the collector's own storage
ia.primaryLoop: Open the library that spans every source, play gapless from the NAS at home and from the cache in the car, and pin the next albums for offline before leaving the house.

music-streaming-3.territory: It is 11pm, the record just ended, and the listener wants to hold onto the opinion before it dissolves. The interface answers like a theater after the house lights drop: near-black, unhurried, the album art the only lit object in the room. Everything else — ratings, reviews, friends — behaves like conversation in the lobby afterward, quiet and worth keeping.

palette.note: Matte theater black, never blue-black; the gold-record accent marks ratings and milestones only, so the album artwork stays the sole source of color on every screen.

music-streaming-3.typography: GT Sectra Display for review text and album titles — serif italics that read like liner notes — with Neue Haas Grotesk for UI chrome so the machinery stays invisible.
music-streaming-3.motif: The spine shelf: every rated album becomes a vinyl spine with your score foil-stamped on it, and the diary is a shelf that visibly grows month by month.

ia.coreObject: The album entry (artwork, your rating, your short review, listen count, and its spine on the shelf)
ia.primaryLoop: Each morning the app surfaces yesterday's listens; you rate the album that stayed with you, and the shelf, the friends feed, and the recap all deepen from that one honest minute.

music-streaming-5.territory: The user is thirty years and six thousand miles from the kitchen where this station always played, listening in a New Jersey car or a California bedroom, and every dropout feels like the line home going dead. The interface answers as a warm dark theater: the station is the performer, the glow is amber like a tuned dial, and reliability is staged as visible stagecraft, not a settings checkbox.

palette.note: Amber behaves like dial light: full glow on the playing station, ember-dim on everything else, and it never blinks off during a reconnect, only breathes.

music-streaming-5.typography: Golos Text carrying Cyrillic, Greek, and Vietnamese with equal dignity, paired with Martian Mono for frequencies and timers; every title is set as a two-line lockup, native script large, Latin transliteration small beneath.
music-streaming-5.motif: The dual-script lockup: song and station names always rendered native-script-over-Latin as a single typographic unit, the product's signature visible on every screen, widget, and CarPlay tile.

notes-pkm-2.territory: The med student is in the lecture hall or on the bus, typing fast and terrified of the second job that awaits tonight: moving everything into Anki. The interface answers like a well-made study desk: warm paper, ink, one yellow marker, and the quiet mechanical satisfaction of a page corner folding itself into a flashcard while they keep writing.

palette.note: The highlighter yellow appears only where a passage has become a card, sweeping semi-transparent over the user's own words, so a glance down any page shows exactly how much of it is already in the review deck.

notes-pkm-2.typography: Lyon Text for the notes themselves and Graphik for chrome and card stats: reading your own notes should feel like a well-set textbook, while the scheduling machinery stays in plain modern type.
notes-pkm-2.motif: The dog-ear fold: when a highlighted passage becomes a card, its corner visibly folds like a turned page corner, and folded corners throughout the notebook mark everything the deck now knows.

ia.coreObject: The note-card pair: a paragraph in your notes and the spaced-repetition card folded out of it, permanently linked
ia.primaryLoop: In class the student types notes and folds key passages into cards with one tap, then clears the due queue in the gaps of the day, returning because the queue is short, honest, and always in their pocket.

notes-pkm-3.territory: Five meetings deep, the consultant can no longer swear who promised what to whom, and the next call starts in four minutes. The interface answers like a master stenographer's desk: paper-quiet, typographically exact, recording with a reliability that never needs checking twice. The one emotion it must never produce is doubt about whether the recorder was actually running.

palette.note: Legal-pad paper warmth with fountain-pen blue-black for actions and links; the recording state alone owns a small steady red dot, never blinking decoration, and the margin rule is printed in a faint vermilion like a real pad.

notes-pkm-3.typography: Lyon Text for transcripts and summaries — a serif built for long-form reading — with Atlas Grotesk for speaker labels, timestamps and controls, so the spoken word and the machinery never share a voice.
notes-pkm-3.motif: The margin rule: every transcript page carries a printed vertical margin line, and decisions, action items and deadlines are pulled across it into the margin as the meeting happens — the app's entire value visible as ink crossing a line.

ia.coreObject: The meeting record (audio, speaker-split transcript, and the margin: decisions, action items, deadlines)
ia.primaryLoop: Before every conversation that matters, one tap starts the recorder; minutes after it ends, the margin holds who promised what by when, and the day's five meetings stop blurring together.

notes-pkm-6.territory: The person has kept a journal for years and carries a quiet dread of the one evening it all disappears. The interface answers with the composure of a well-run archive: paper, ink, and daily visible proof of safekeeping, a room where nothing is ever thrown away.

palette.note: Color behaves like ink on paper: navy is reserved for the day's stamp, links and verified marks, never poured as a background behind text.

notes-pkm-6.typography: Williams Caslon Text sets every entry like a printed page while Atlas Grotesk whispers the chrome; the writing always looks typeset, the app never louder than the words.
notes-pkm-6.motif: The triplicate stamp: three small squares in the corner of today's page that ink themselves in, one by one, as each of the day's three backups lands.

ia.coreObject: The entry: one dated page with its mood note and its three verified copies
ia.primaryLoop: Write today's page, watch the triplicate stamp fill in, and get pulled back tomorrow by pages from this same date in earlier years.

notes-pkm-7.territory: Mid-meeting, a thought arrives faster than any app can open, and the fear is losing it in transit between tools. The interface answers like a craftsman's bench: the blank page is already lying there when you reach for it, and filing is one motion of the hand. Everything about it is paper, graphite, and restraint, a tool that disappears into the gesture.

palette.note: The page stays ink-on-paper monochrome; each destination owns a colored screen edge (Obsidian violet, Todoist red, Mail blue, Calendar green), and the workshop orange is reserved for the app's own actions.

notes-pkm-7.typography: iA Writer Quattro on the writing surface, the most honest capture typeface there is, with Inter in the chrome staying out of its way.
notes-pkm-7.motif: Pigeonhole edges: the four edges of the screen are the filing system, each glowing faintly with its destination's color as a note is dragged toward it, like sliding paper into a labeled slot.

ia.coreObject: The draft: a captured thought waiting to be routed somewhere that isn't this app
ia.primaryLoop: Open to an already-blank page, jot or dictate, swipe toward an edge to file it, and sweep the leftovers each evening.

notes-pkm-8.territory: An analyst or lawyer is buried under fifty PDFs, anxious about missing the one line that decides the matter and uneasy about where these confidential files travel. The interface answers with the hush of a law library reading room: paper warmth, footnote discipline, and provenance on every claim. Nothing flashes, nothing guesses, everything is signed with a page number.

palette.note: Ivory paper carries everything; the brick-red accent is reserved exclusively for citation markers and the sealed-vault indicator, so red always means 'this is sourced' or 'this is private'.

notes-pkm-8.typography: Tiempos Text for answers and document excerpts, Söhne for UI chrome and citation chips; the serif body makes machine answers read like a drafted brief while superscript numerals do the real talking.
notes-pkm-8.motif: The citation tab: every answer sentence carries a small brick-red superscript numeral that physically tethers to a paper-edge tab peeking from the right margin, and pulling the tab slides the actual source page into view.

ia.coreObject: The session: a question-and-answer thread bound to a fixed pile of sources, where every answer sentence is anchored to a document and page

notes-pkm-9.territory: The writer has eleven minutes on the subway and one fear: friction between them and the sentence. The interface answers like a well-kept writing desk, warm paper, real book typography, tools that stay in the drawer until reached for. It should feel closer to a bound manuscript in progress than to software.

palette.note: The page is paper-warm and matte, and oxblood is used the way an editor uses a red pencil, sparingly, on chapter numerals and the daily goal ring.

notes-pkm-9.typography: Tiempos Text for the manuscript itself and Untitled Sans for chrome, so the writing looks typeset like a book while every count and control stays plain and small.
notes-pkm-9.motif: The folio margin: chapter numerals and running word counts live in a hairline left margin like printer's folios, so the manuscript always reads as a book being made.

nutrition-calories-1.territory: A person with diabetes finishing lunch and already half-dreading the number their sensor will show in ninety minutes, tired of guessing which food did it. The interface answers with clinical freshness: white, exact, unjudging, where every plate is simply paired with the curve it caused and the data slowly turns dread into a personal map of safe food.

palette.note: Clinical white with a calm teal-green for glucose curves and in-range fills; the personal food verdicts use muted leaf #3E8E5A, ochre #C79A2A and clay #B65C3F dots, quiet enough that a red-dot food reads as information, never as scolding.

nutrition-calories-1.typography: Fraunces in its low-contrast text weights for meal names, giving food its warmth, over Söhne Mono for every mg/dL value and minute count, because the numbers here are medical and must look it.
nutrition-calories-1.motif: The meal shadow: every logged plate casts a 180-minute glucose sparkline directly beneath it like a shadow, so food and consequence are one inseparable object everywhere in the app.

ia.coreObject: The meal entry paired with its 3-hour glucose response: peak, time in range, minutes back to target
ia.primaryLoop: Log each meal in a couple of taps, let the sensor fill in the shadow over the next three hours, and watch a personal green-yellow-red food map sharpen toward the 30-day ranking.

nutrition-calories-3.territory: It is Sunday afternoon and the week is about to happen to you: six dinners, two kids, a budget, and a fridge you half-remember. The interface answers with the brisk, appetizing confidence of a good market stall, everything laid out, priced, and fresh, so planning feels like abundance being organized rather than a chore being endured. Honest numbers, zero guilt, no diary to confess into.

palette.note: A clean white-tile kitchen where food photography supplies almost all the color; the single tomato red is reserved for the one action that matters on each screen and for the budget number when it is safe.

nutrition-calories-3.typography: Söhne for UI and tabular budget figures, Tiempos Headline for recipe names, so dishes read like a menu worth cooking while quantities and prices stay strict and columnar.
nutrition-calories-3.motif: The rotation ring: every recipe thumbnail wears a thin 28-segment ring that fills as the no-repeat clock runs down, and a dish with an open ring is simply not offered.

nutrition-calories-4.territory: The dietitian opens this between back-to-back consults, running a solo practice out of spreadsheets and a messaging app, half worried some client quietly stopped logging two weeks ago. The interface answers as a clinical workspace with a warm bedside manner: crisp white, honest tabular numbers, and a roster that lets her triage twenty clients in the time a coffee cools.

nutrition-calories-4.typography: Graphik runs the workspace with tabular figures wherever a nutrient number appears, and the client-side diary uses the same family one size larger so both halves feel like one practice.
nutrition-calories-4.motif: The seven-dot week: every client carries a strip of seven dots, one per day of diary logging, filled or hollow, readable from across the room and repeated everywhere their name appears.

nutrition-calories-5.territory: A strength athlete four weeks into a cut opens the app on Monday knowing the target may change, and what they dread is not the change but the silence around it. The interface answers like a competent colleague handing over a signed memo: clean clinical surfaces, every number footnoted, every recalculation written out in plain sentences with a disagree button attached. Energy comes from confidence in the math, not from confetti.

palette.note: Cool lab neutrality with one cobalt for the current phase's live numbers; the accent shifts hue by phase, cobalt on a cut, amber on a bulk, slate green at maintenance, so the whole app quietly wears the phase you are in.

nutrition-calories-5.typography: Charter for the algorithm's written memos so the math reads like a colleague's note rather than a system alert, with IBM Plex Mono for every gram, calorie, and kilogram in strict tabular columns.
nutrition-calories-5.motif: The footnote: every target number on screen carries a small superscript marker that unfolds into the exact plain-English derivation behind it, so there is no number in the app without a visible paper trail.

ia.coreObject: The weekly target set (calories, protein, carbs, fat) with its attached derivation memo and the phase it belongs to
ia.primaryLoop: Weigh in and log meals daily, read the Monday memo explaining the week's recalculation, accept or override it, and watch the phase plan advance toward its transition date.

screens.purpose: The core mechanic at its moment: the weekly recalculation delivered as a signed, disagreeable note.
screens.hero: A full-width Charter memo with the change stated in the first line.
screens.data: Memo, Jul 20: Your target drops 50 kcal to 2,290. Why: trend weight fell 0.31 kg this week, slightly under your 0.33 kg goal. Expenditure estimate: 2,905 kcal from 7 weigh-ins and 7 full logs. Protein holds at 185g, the cut comes from carbs. Buttons: Accept · Disagree and set manually.

screens.purpose: The disagree flow honored fully: manual targets with the algorithm noting, not fighting, the decision.

screens.data: Manual: 2,350 kcal, your entry, versus suggested 2,290. Note field: big squat day Thursday. System line: Your override runs this week. Next Monday's memo will use your actual intake, not the suggestion. No warning colors anywhere.

screens.title: The floor holds
screens.purpose: The safety mechanic at its earning moment: the math wanted to go lower and the app declines, offering a diet break instead.
screens.hero: A memo variant with a drawn horizontal floor line the target rests on.
screens.data: Memo, Sep 7: The math points to 1,890 kcal. Your floor is 2,000, so the target holds at 2,000. You have been in deficit 9 weeks; consider a 2-week diet break at maintenance, 2,780 kcal. Buttons: Start diet break · Hold at floor. Footnote: how your floor was set, editable in Settings.

screens.data: Plan: cut ends Aug 10 at 79.5 kg. Reverse ramp: +150 kcal per week for 3 weeks to estimated maintenance 2,780. Each step arrives with its own memo. Rules chip row: Cut rules · Maintenance rules · Bulk rules, each with different recalculation speeds, tap to read.

screens.title: Expected water, not fat

screens.hero: The weight chart with a shaded cycle band over the bump.
screens.data: This week: scale up 0.8 kg. Label on the bump: cycle day 21, typical water for you. Trend line underneath: still minus 0.28 kg. Memo excerpt: No target change. This rise matches your last 3 cycles and is excluded from the fat trend.

screens.data: Copy Thursday: 4 meals. Today's target is 60 kcal lower, so portions scale 0.97x: rice 180g becomes 174g, oats 90g becomes 87g, protein foods held at 100 percent by rule. Line: protein is never scaled down first. Button: Add all 4 meals.

nutrition-calories-6.territory: The person is holding a lab report that says ferritin 11 ng/mL and feels a low hum of worry mixed with determination to fix it before the retest. The interface answers with clinical calm and kitchen warmth: honest numbers set like a lab report, food shown like a cookbook, and a visible finish line at the retest date.

nutrition-calories-7.territory: The user is three days past an injection, staring at a half-finished 200-calorie yogurt, tired of apps scolding them to eat more. The interface answers with clinical warmth: the calm of a good dietitian who understands the medication, celebrates 40 grams of protein on a tiny appetite, and never raises an alarm about the calories. Bright, appetizing, and private like a medical chart that happens to be beautiful.

palette.note: Warm clinical white with apricot carrying protein progress and a soft leaf-brown #8A6F3C for fiber, while calories live in quiet gray footnote type with no red states anywhere in the app.

nutrition-calories-7.typography: GT Walsheim for headings with its rounded medical-brand friendliness, and Inter with tabular numerals for grams and doses, so the chart-like data stays exact without feeling like an audit.
nutrition-calories-7.motif: The twin arc: protein and fiber drawn as two nested arcs that fill toward the day's goal regardless of how small the portions were, with calories printed underneath in footnote gray, a hierarchy no generic tracker has.

ia.coreObject: The day (meals, protein and fiber arcs, dose position, symptoms)
ia.primaryLoop: After each small meal the user logs it in seconds and watches the twin arcs advance, and they return nightly because the diary is the only place where food, dose day, and symptoms line up into a pattern their doctor can use.

password-manager-2.territory: The person is standing at a checkout or staring at their banking app's login, master of their own KeePass file yet humiliated by a fill button that works half the time. The interface answers with archival calm: warm paper, stamped confirmations, everything explainable, like a records office where every failure has a filed reason and a fix. Its dignity comes from candor, the app would rather diagnose itself than pretend.

palette.note: Oxide red is the ink of the stamp, appearing only when something is confirmed, bound, or diagnosed, so its every appearance certifies a fact.

password-manager-2.typography: Spectral for headings and explanatory prose, JetBrains Mono for usernames, TOTP codes, and file paths, pairing archival seriousness with the mono honesty KeePass people live in.
password-manager-2.motif: The rubber stamp: successful autofills, app bindings, and completed diagnoses each land a small pressed stamp mark, slightly imperfect like real ink, turning reliability into a visible paper trail.

ia.coreObject: Your KeePass file, opened in place from wherever you keep it, with per-entry bindings to the apps they unlock
ia.primaryLoop: The user autofills logins in native apps all day, and every fill either lands a stamp or opens a diagnosis that ends in a fix, so reliability compounds instead of eroding.

password-manager-4.territory: The person is the one adult in the family who thinks about the worst day, and using this app feels like putting papers in order at a solid desk after everyone is asleep. The interface answers with the dignity of a private bank at dusk, deep ink and brass, unhurried and ceremonial where it matters. Nothing here is playful, because the envelope at its center is a promise made to people who will one day open it in grief.

palette.note: Brass is spent only on keys, seals, and the envelope, so the most valuable objects in the vault literally carry the metal.

password-manager-4.typography: Financier Display for section titles and the envelope ceremony, Founders Grotesk for lists and controls, giving the app the register of an estate document rather than a tech product.
password-manager-4.motif: The two-key seal: the inheritance envelope is drawn as a brass-sealed envelope with two keyholes, and every state of it, sealed, requested, waiting, opened, is a change to that one emblem.

ia.coreObject: The family vault, split into private sections per person, one shared section, and the sealed inheritance envelope
ia.primaryLoop: Day to day the family autofills from shared and private sections, and the owner returns every few months to keep the envelope and its instructions current, which is the actual product being bought.

password-manager-5.territory: The person arrives freshly frightened: their password manager just showed '42 compromised' and then went silent. The interface answers with bank-vault composure, the register of a trust officer laying a short document on a desk: here is what actually matters, here is the order, we will be done this evening. No red sirens, no counters of doom, just paper, ink and a plan.

palette.note: Ink on warm paper with one bank-blue accent, and a deep verdigris green appears solely as the seal of a completed step, never as decoration.

password-manager-5.typography: National 2 keeps interface text precise and unexcitable, Spectral sets the plan's step headings with the gravity of a well-set legal document.
password-manager-5.motif: The wax seal: every completed step is stamped with a small embossed circular seal, and the final report is a page of seals, proof the risk was actually closed rather than stared at.

ia.coreObject: The audit: one imported password export turned into a prioritized fix plan
ia.primaryLoop: This is a one-evening tool, not a daily app: import, work the five-step plan to the last seal, get the report, and come back only when the reminder says it is time to check again.

screens.title: Bring the list that scared you
screens.purpose: Onboarding step one: import the export file from whichever manager raised the alarm.
screens.hero: A document tray accepting a file, with the source logos rendered as quiet monochrome stamps
screens.data: Copy: 'Export your passwords from Apple Passwords, 1Password, Chrome or any manager as a CSV, then drop it here.' Per-source guides: 'How to export from Apple Passwords (30 seconds)'. Button: Choose file. Footnote: 'The file is read on this device.'

screens.title: What leaves your phone
screens.purpose: Onboarding step two: state the k-anonymity mechanism plainly before anything is checked, because this audience was just burned by opacity.
screens.hero: A diagram of a password reduced to a truncated fingerprint, with the rest visibly staying on-device
screens.data: Copy: 'To check a password we send only the first 5 characters of its hash, a fingerprint fragment shared by thousands of passwords. Your passwords never leave this device, and nothing is kept after the session.' Button: I understand, run the check.

screens.title: Nothing to audit yet
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state for someone who opened the app before exporting anything.
screens.hero: An empty desk blotter with a single instruction card on it
screens.data: Header: 'No audit yet.' Card: 'Step 1: get your export. We will wait.' Three linked walkthroughs: 'Apple Passwords', '1Password', 'Chrome'. Note: 'First 10 entries are checked free, the full audit is a one-time $10.'

screens.title: Checking your entries
screens.purpose: The working state while entries are compared against breach corpora, calm and specific instead of a spinner.
screens.hero: A progress ledger filling line by line
screens.data: 'Checking 214 entries against Have I Been Pwned and 3 breach corpora. 131 of 214 done. Found so far: 42 exposed.' Footnote: 'About 40 seconds left. Fingerprint fragments only, remember.'

screens.title: Your plan, not your list
screens.purpose: Main screen mid-use: the 42-item scare collapsed into a short ordered plan built on the attack chain.
screens.hero: Five Spectral-headed steps in a single column, the first one open, seals waiting empty beside each
screens.data: Header: '42 exposed. Realistically: 5 steps tonight.' Steps: '1. Gmail, everything else resets through it', '2. Chase, your money', '3. Amazon, card on file', '4. PayPal, card on file', '5. Dropbox, holds your tax PDFs'. Below: '9 to do this month, 28 archived as low risk.'

screens.title: Step one: Gmail
screens.purpose: The step detail that walks the fix: why this one is first, the direct link, and the done checkbox.
screens.hero: One card with the reasoning paragraph and a single blue action
screens.data: Copy: 'Your Gmail password appeared in the 2024 combolist breach. Every account below resets through this inbox, so it goes first.' Button: 'Open Gmail password change'. Checklist: 'Changed the password', 'Turned on 2-step verification (recommended)'. Mark done stamps the seal.

screens.title: The dead accounts
screens.purpose: The filter mechanic: old forums and one-off shops moved to low priority so they do not bloat the plan.
screens.hero: A stack of faded entries sliding into an 'Archive' folder
screens.data: Header: '28 entries look dead.' Rows: 'vBulletin bike forum, last used 2013', 'flash-game site, 2011', 'hotel wifi portal, 2019'. Actions per row: 'Keep archived' or 'Actually matters, move to plan'. Footnote: 'Archived entries stay in the report, marked low risk.'

screens.title: The page of seals
screens.purpose: The final report: what got closed, what remains, and when to come back, the emotional payoff of the evening.
screens.hero: A certificate-like page with five embossed seals in a row
screens.data: 'Audit closed, October 12. 5 of 5 priority steps sealed. 9 medium entries scheduled for this month. 28 archived. Real risk closed in 1 hour 40 minutes.' Row: 'Remind me to re-check: in 6 months, January 2027.' Button: 'Save report PDF'.

screens.title: Session cleared
screens.purpose: The trust state after closing the report: demonstrate that imported data is gone.
screens.hero: The desk blotter empty again, a shredded-strip mark where the file card used to be
screens.data: Copy: 'Your import and all check results were deleted from this device. We keep only your report PDF if you saved it, and your reminder date.' Rows: 'Reminder: January 2027', 'Nothing else stored.'

screens.title: Clean bill
screens.purpose: The alternate result state: an audit that finds nothing must feel like a result, not an anticlimax.
screens.hero: A single large seal on an otherwise empty page
screens.data: '0 of 214 entries found in any breach corpus. No plan needed.' Sub: 'Your manager's alert may have been stale, this check ran today against corpora updated this week.' Row: 'Re-check reminder: in 6 months.'

screens.title: The full audit, once
screens.purpose: Paywall at the moment of proven value: the first 10 entries already checked free, the rest unlocked with a single payment.
screens.hero: A quiet invoice-styled card, priced like a document fee rather than a subscription
screens.data: 'First 10 entries checked free: 3 exposed already found. Unlock all 214: $10, once.' Included: 'Full plan, direct fix links, dead-account filter, sealed report.' Explicitly absent: 'No subscription, no monitoring, no renewal.' Links: 'Restore purchase', 'Terms'.

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: The few controls a one-evening tool honestly needs.
screens.hero: A short grouped list, half of it about deletion
screens.data: Rows: 'Re-check reminder: January 2027, edit', 'Breach sources: Have I Been Pwned + 3 corpora, view list', 'Delete session data now', 'Delete saved reports', 'Restore purchase'. Footnote: 'No account exists. There is nothing to log out of.'

password-manager-6.territory: The person has been burned by every iOS update, watching their own Dropbox-hosted vault drift out of sync, and they open this app braced for disappointment. The interface answers like a precision instrument on a clean bench: cool, exact, every claim about sync backed by a visible receipt. Trust here is not a mood, it is a status line with a revision hash on it.

palette.note: Instrument blue marks sync state and nothing else, so a glance at any screen answers the only question this audience has: is my file safe right now.

password-manager-6.typography: IBM Plex Sans for the interface with IBM Plex Mono for filenames, revision hashes, and snapshot timestamps, because this audience trusts monospace receipts more than adjectives.
password-manager-6.motif: The snapshot rings: the local history of the last 30 database states drawn as thin concentric rings around the vault icon, like tree rings, one added per change, any ring tappable to roll back.

ia.coreObject: Your own database file, living in iCloud Drive, Dropbox, WebDAV, or a local folder, never on our servers
ia.primaryLoop: The user autofills all day across iPhone and iPad while the app quietly reconciles record-level edits into their own cloud file, and the visible sync receipt is what keeps them from ever checking manually again.

screens.title: The merge, witnessed
screens.purpose: The moment sync earns its keep: edits from two devices reconciled at record level, shown, not asserted.
screens.hero: Two device columns, iPhone and iPad, with three record rows flowing into one merged column.
screens.data: '3 records reconciled, 0 conflicts.' iPad changed Interactive Brokers password Mar 5, 9:14 AM. iPhone added entry Peloton Mar 5, 9:20 AM. iPhone edited NAS note. Result written as rev 9a1d07. Line: 'You were never asked to choose a file version.'

screens.title: The empty-file rescue
screens.purpose: The disaster this audience has actually lived through, defused by the snapshot rings.
screens.hero: An amber-bordered card, 'Dropbox returned a 0 KB file. Your data is safe.', above the rings with one ring highlighted.
screens.data: 'Refused to overwrite local copy.' Snapshots available: today 11:42 AM (412 entries), 9:03 AM (412), yesterday 10:51 PM (411). Buttons: 'Restore 11:42 AM snapshot', 'Inspect first'. Footer: 'Snapshots live on this device, last 30 states.'

screens.title: Offline on the train
screens.purpose: Show that no connectivity means queued, not broken.
screens.hero: The status bar in neutral gray, 'Offline, 2 changes queued', with the rest of the app fully usable.
screens.data: Queued: edited Proton Mail password 8:12 AM, added entry 'office door code' 8:26 AM. Line: 'Will reconcile with Dropbox when you are back. Nothing is lost by waiting.'

screens.title: Beta watch changelog
screens.purpose: The public receipt that this developer tests on iOS betas before users get hurt.
screens.hero: A changelog list styled like release notes, newest iOS beta pinned on top.
screens.data: 'iOS 27 beta 3: iCloud Drive file coordination changed. Broke silent saves. Fixed in 2.4.1, shipped Jun 30.' 'iOS 27 beta 1: no issues found, 412-entry test vault, 200 sync cycles.' Subscribe toggle: 'Notify me when a beta breaks something'.

screens.title: Export, no conditions
screens.purpose: The one-screen full export that proves the exit door is real and always open.
screens.hero: A single button, 'Export entire database', above the format list, no warnings, no upsell.
screens.data: Formats: KDBX 4, CSV, JSON. Includes: all 412 entries, 2FA secrets, attachments. Destination: Files, AirDrop. Line: 'Works on the free tier too. It is your data.'

screens.title: Entry 51, the paywall
screens.purpose: Convert at the natural threshold with the one-time deal this audience deliberately seeks out.
screens.hero: A plain receipt-style card: 'You have 50 free entries. The lifetime license removes the cap.'
screens.data: $29 once. Includes: unlimited entries, all storage backends, snapshots, every 2.x update. Stated plainly: 'A major paid version comes every 3 to 4 years, discounted for owners. Nothing you bought gets taken away.' Restore purchase link directly under the price.

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: Storage, snapshots, and lock behavior, written like a spec sheet.
screens.hero: A grouped list with the storage location and its mono path on top.
screens.data: Database: Dropbox/Apps/vault/family.vaultdb. Snapshots kept: 30 (about 18 MB). Lock after: 2 min. Unlock: Face ID, master password weekly. Beta changelog notifications: on. App version 2.4.1.

password-manager-7.territory: Standing at a rental counter or a clinic front desk with the wallet at home and mild adrenaline rising. The interface answers like a bank vault opening on schedule: unhurried, brass-and-ink certainty that the document is exactly where it was left, and will still be there ten years from now.

palette.note: Deep ink lets the documents' own photos carry the color; brass is reserved for card edges and the unlock moment, the way a vault saves its shine for the door.

password-manager-7.typography: Financier Display gives card titles their ledger gravity, Suisse Int'l keeps field values legible at arm's length when the phone is handed across a counter.
password-manager-7.motif: The brass-clipped sleeve: every document is a physical card sliding out of a labeled sleeve with a brass corner, and the pull-out gesture is the app's signature move.

ia.primaryLoop: At a counter, unlock with Face ID and slide the right card out in under five seconds; at home, the app quietly flags what expires next.

password-manager-8.territory: A 75-year-old opening the app to find the pharmacy login, a little braced for failure because software usually wins. The interface answers like a well-lit page of a familiar notebook: nothing moves, nothing pops up, the letters are big enough to trust on the first read, and help is a person, not a chatbot.

palette.note: Warm paper with AAA contrast everywhere; the single masthead blue appears only on the one tappable action per screen, so there is never a question of where to press.

password-manager-8.typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible at newspaper-headline sizes throughout, a typeface designed for low vision doing the accessibility work the layout promises.
password-manager-8.motif: The ruled line: every entry sits on one wide ruled row like a lined notebook page, because the app is honestly replacing the notebook in the kitchen drawer.
