weather-apps-1.territory: It's 8 pm and a charter captain has six paying guests booked for 7 am; the decision to run or cancel is his alone, and being wrong costs either the fee or the safety of people on his boat. The interface answers like a trusted first mate reading a paper chart under the wheelhouse lamp: unhurried, exact, committed to a call. The sky sets the stakes, but the chart — calm, drawn, annotated — is what he steers by.

palette.note: NOAA-chart cream and ink; the marine teal marks open, runnable water and hours, while unsafe hours wear the brick-and-hatch treatment of charted shoals — the palette is literally the chart's hazard language.

weather-apps-1.typography: DIN 2014 sets every wind speed, gust and tide numeral like an instrument face, while Charter italic carries place names and notes the way a paper nautical chart labels its waters.
weather-apps-1.motif: The channel: every day renders as a horizontal waterway where safe hours are open water and unsafe hours are hatched shoal marks, so the go-window reads like a passage you can steer through.

ia.coreObject: The spot — one saved coastal point with your vessel's thresholds laid over its wind, swell and tide
ia.primaryLoop: Check tomorrow's channel the evening before, make the go or no-go call in ten seconds, then compare forecast to what the water actually did — the app earns tomorrow's trust by being right today.

weather-apps-2.territory: Saturday, 7am, coffee going cold while a pilot decides whether today is a flying day — a decision with real consequences made in a kitchen, not a cockpit. The interface answers with the calm of a good flight instructor: aviation units, no atmosphere theater, a straight verdict first and the evidence beneath it. The sky sets the stakes; the screen stays clinical so judgment stays clear.

palette.note: Cool paper white like a sectional chart margin; the accent is sectional-chart magenta for interactive elements, while flight-category colors (VFR green, MVFR blue, IFR red) are reserved strictly for their FAA meanings and never decorate anything.

weather-apps-2.typography: B612 and B612 Mono throughout — the typeface Airbus commissioned for cockpit displays — so raw METARs, altitudes and winds read with instrument-panel legibility at arm's length.
weather-apps-2.motif: The flight progress strip: every briefing is a stack of ATC-style paper strips, one per airport, and the go/no-go verdict is a strip stamped across the top.

ia.coreObject: The briefing (departure, destination, alternate: decoded weather, winds aloft, and a VFR window verdict)
ia.primaryLoop: The night before or over breakfast, the pilot pulls one briefing for the planned hop, reads the verdict strip, and either blocks the flying window or goes back to bed with a clear conscience.

screens.title: Your home field
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 1: set the airport you actually fly from and what you fly.
screens.hero: A single identifier input rendered as a blank progress strip
screens.data: Field: KPAO (Palo Alto). Aircraft: Cessna 172S. Note: 'Everything in knots, feet, statute miles, and inches of mercury. No conversions, ever.'

screens.title: Your personal minima
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 2: the ceilings and visibility below which the app calls it a no-go for you specifically.
screens.hero: Two large steppers on one card, pre-filled with conservative defaults
screens.data: Ceiling: 3,000 ft AGL. Visibility: 5 SM. Max surface wind: 15 kt, gust 20. Line beneath: 'Stricter than legal VFR on purpose. Adjust as your hours grow.'

screens.title: No routes yet
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state: one input away from a first briefing.
screens.hero: An empty strip bay with a ghosted example strip showing what's coming
screens.data: 'Type two identifiers and get a briefing in 10 seconds.' Placeholder: 'KPAO KMRY'. Below: 'Recent fields near you: KPAO, KSQL, KHWD'.

screens.title: Saturday's briefing
screens.purpose: Main screen mid-use: the whole go/no-go answer for KPAO → KMRY in one stack.
screens.hero: The verdict strip stamped across the top in flight-category color
screens.data: 'VFR window today: 10:00–15:30 local. After 15:30, marine stratus returns to the coast.' Strips below: KPAO — VFR, 29008KT, FEW025. KMRY — MVFR until 10:00 (OVC008), then VFR. Confidence: High.

screens.title: METAR, decoded
screens.purpose: Raw and plain-English side by side, so the abbreviations stop living only in your head.
screens.hero: A split card: monospaced raw text left, decoded sentences right, line-matched
screens.data: Raw: 'KMRY 141156Z 29008KT 10SM FEW008 SCT200 16/12 A3002'. Decode: 'Wind 290° at 8 kt. Visibility 10 SM. Few clouds at 800 ft — watch this one, it's the marine layer remnant. Temp 16, dewpoint 12, spread 4°C. Altimeter 30.02.'

screens.title: TAF against your minima
screens.purpose: The forecast timeline with your personal limits drawn on it, not just legal ones.
screens.hero: A horizontal timeline strip with your minima as a magenta rule across it
screens.data: KMRY TAF: OVC008 until 1800Z, then SCT015 → FEW025. Your 3,000 ft line crossed at 10:00 local. Callout: 'Legal VFR from 09:20, your minima from 10:00. The gap is where scud-running lives.'

screens.title: Winds aloft, two models
screens.purpose: The disagreement flag: when GFS and NAM diverge, say so instead of averaging it away.
screens.hero: A table of altitudes with both model columns and an amber flag where they split
screens.data: 6,000 ft: GFS 290/14 kt, NAM 300/22 kt — flagged: '8 kt disagreement, headwind component differs by 11 kt on this route'. 9,000 ft: both ~300/18. Note: 'Models converge after 18Z run. Re-check at 11:00.'

screens.title: Clouds along the route
screens.purpose: The route profile: ceiling and visibility between the two fields, not just at them.
screens.hero: A side-view terrain profile with cloud bases drawn to scale over the route line
screens.data: KPAO → KMRY, 62 NM. Ceilings: 2,500 ft over the Santa Cruz ridge until 10:30, unlimited after. Visibility 10+ SM throughout. Note: 'Ridge crossing at 3,000 ft clears your minima only after the stratus burns off.'

screens.title: Three strips: the full picture
screens.purpose: Departure, destination, alternate in one glance — the classic instructor's habit, made default.
screens.hero: Three progress strips stacked, alternate slightly indented
screens.data: KPAO (dep): VFR all day. KMRY (dest): VFR from 10:00. KSNS (alt): VFR now, winds 320/12. Footer: 'Alternate stays VFR through 17:00 in all models.'

screens.title: The night-before check

screens.hero: The same verdict strip on a near-black panel, text in low-glare warm white
screens.data: 'Tomorrow, Sunday: VFR window likely 09:30–16:00, confidence Medium (TAF amendment expected 06:00). Winds aloft light. Wake-up check scheduled 06:30.'

screens.title: Cached in the hangar

screens.hero: The briefing stack with a timestamp band across the top instead of the verdict
screens.data: 'Cached 07:42, now 09:10 — 1h 28m old. METARs update hourly; treat ceilings as stale. Last known: KMRY OVC008 lifting.' Button: 'Retry when signal returns'.

screens.title: Weather is a line item
screens.purpose: Paywall after the third free briefing, priced against the budget row pilots already have.

weather-apps-3.territory: It is 5:30am in the yard and the question is whether to cut hay today, a call worth a thousand dollars either way. The interface answers like a trusted almanac crossed with the rain gauge nailed to the fence post: warm paper, big honest numbers for your dirt, not the city's. No moods, no animations — a neighbor who checked the instruments and tells it to you straight.

palette.note: Almanac cream with the slate-blue of measured water as the only accent; frost warnings alone may go ice-white on deep navy, and nothing is ever colored for decoration.

weather-apps-3.typography: Tiempos Text for forecasts and field notes — sturdy, bookish, almanac-grade — with Basis Grotesque tabular figures for rainfall totals and temperatures that must be read in one glance from a moving tractor.
weather-apps-3.motif: The rain gauge: a vertical gauge glyph filled to the measured tenth of an inch anchors every field card, echoing the physical gauge on the fence the farmer already trusts.

ia.coreObject: The field (a GPS polygon with its own rainfall total, frost risk, work windows, and season log)
ia.primaryLoop: Every morning before first light the farmer checks how much water actually fell on each field and what the next three days allow, then commits the day's labor to cutting, planting, or waiting.

screens.title: Pin your first field
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 1: drop a pin (or trace the boundary) on the actual acreage, not the town.
screens.hero: A satellite map with a hand-drawn polygon over a hay field
screens.data: Field name: 'North 40'. Traced: 38.2 acres. Note: 'Forecasts and rainfall totals will be computed for this polygon — the nearest town is 11 miles away and gets different weather.'

screens.title: What grows here
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 2: crop and planting date, so degree days and frost stakes mean something.
screens.hero: Two simple pickers on a paper card
screens.data: North 40: alfalfa, second cutting. Home Garden: tomatoes, planted May 12. Line: 'Frost alerts will use ground-level temperature. Tomatoes get warned at 36°F, alfalfa doesn't panic until 28°F.'

screens.title: First morning
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state: the gauge exists but hasn't measured anything for you yet.
screens.hero: An empty rain gauge with a pencil line at zero
screens.data: 'Your first rainfall total lands tomorrow at 5:00am. Until then, here's the 3-day outlook for North 40: dry, dry, 60% showers Thursday.' Tip: 'Have a fence-post gauge? Enter its readings to sharpen ours.'

screens.title: Today, 5:30am
screens.purpose: Main screen mid-use: what fell overnight and what today permits, before boots go on.
screens.hero: The North 40 gauge filled to 0.7 in, drawn large enough to read across the kitchen
screens.data: 'North 40 caught 0.7 in overnight (town station showed 0.1 — your cell got the heavy band).' Today: drying, wind 8 mph, no rain until Thursday 60%. Flag: 'Too wet to rake before noon.'

screens.title: Where that number comes from
screens.purpose: The trust screen: show the cross-referencing so the total is believable, not oracular.
screens.hero: A small map of the field with the three sources plotted and weighted
screens.data: 0.7 in = radar estimate 0.65 in over your polygon, CoCoRaHS station 2.1 mi NE reported 0.72 in, your fence gauge last calibrated Jun 28 (within 0.05 of us since). 'When sources disagree by more than 0.2 in, we show the range, not a fake average.'

screens.title: Frost, Friday night
screens.purpose: The night warning state: ground-level frost probability, delivered in time to cover the seedlings.
screens.hero: A deep-navy full-screen card, ice-white type, the one dark moment in the app
screens.data: 'Friday night: 70% frost probability at Home Garden. Ground-level low 28°F (shelter height will read 34°F — your phone's weather app will say no frost. It measures at 6 ft. Your tomatoes live at 6 in).' Action: 'Remind me Friday 6pm to cover.'

screens.title: The haying window
screens.purpose: The core money mechanic: three-plus consecutive dry days, with honest model agreement.
screens.hero: A horizontal band of seven day-columns, the dry run highlighted like a good stretch in a ledger
screens.data: 'Cut window: Wednesday–Saturday. 4 dry days, reliability High — 3 of 3 models agree through Friday, 2 of 3 on Saturday.' Dew note: 'Wednesday morning dew heavy, mow after 10am.' Last window this reliable: 12 days ago.

screens.title: All fields
screens.purpose: Multi-field view: each parcel with its own gauge and one-line verdict.
screens.hero: A column of field cards, each led by its miniature gauge
screens.data: North 40 (alfalfa): 0.7 in, rake after noon. Creek Bottom (pasture): 1.1 in, stay off with equipment 2 days. Home Garden (tomatoes): 0.6 in, skip tonight's irrigation, frost watch Friday.

screens.title: Season log
screens.purpose: The ledger that settles arguments in February: what actually happened this season.
screens.hero: A ruled table, almanac-style, one row per week
screens.data: Home Garden since May 12: rainfall 11.3 in, growing degree days 1,240 (base 50°F), frost events 2 (May 19, Jun 2), irrigation skipped 9 times on our call. Export: PDF for the co-op agronomist.

screens.data: 'Operation plan: $149/year — unlimited fields, frost alerts, work windows, season logs, phone-line support in season.' 'Garden plan: $29.99/year — 2 fields, frost alerts, rainfall totals.' Line: 'One rained-on cutting costs more than a decade of this.' Link: 'Restore purchase'. 30-day trial, no card required.

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: Units, alert timing, and gauge calibration — the workshop wall of the app.
screens.hero: A grouped list with the calibration card on top
screens.data: Units: inches / °F (mm available). Morning summary: 5:00am. Frost alerts: evening before + 2h before minimum. Fence gauge calibration: 6 readings entered, model bias corrected +0.04 in. Data area: 3 fields, 41 acres.

weather-apps-5.territory: The user is a foreman at 5:40 in the morning deciding whether eight people drive to a job site, with a concrete pour and a payroll day riding on the call. The interface answers like jobsite signage: flat, high-contrast, glanceable through a windshield, with exactly one verdict per site and colors that mean go, caution, and get down. The sky sets the mood only in the sense that the strip turns red when it should.

palette.note: The day strip owns three fixed meanings, work green, caution amber, stop red, and the safety-orange accent is reserved for actions, never for weather.

weather-apps-5.typography: Barlow Semi Condensed throughout, the highway-signage DNA doing the legibility work, set bold and oversized for verdicts so 'WORK 7–2' reads from a truck dashboard.
weather-apps-5.motif: The work window strip: every day rendered as one horizontal band of green, amber, and red hour blocks, the same strip on the main screen, the alert, the log, and the widget.

ia.coreObject: The job site (an exact address with crew thresholds and its own hour-by-hour verdict strip)
ia.primaryLoop: Check the 5:40am verdict per site, dispatch or hold the crew, and let lightning radius alerts run the day; downtime logs itself for the paper trail

weather-apps-6.territory: Keys in hand at the door, forty seconds to decide: bike or bus, go now or wait it out. The interface answers before it is even opened, a glance at the home screen that already looked two hours ahead. Inside, it feels like standing under the sky itself: the light of the UI shifts with conditions, but the answer is always the same shape, a line and a number of minutes.

palette.note: The interface tints with the sky, slate before rain and pale gold when clear, but rain cells and the arrival line are always the same unmistakable blue.

weather-apps-6.typography: Archivo, tight and signage-like with tabular numerals, because the entire product is one big number of minutes read at arm's length.
weather-apps-6.motif: The arrival line: a thread drawn from the leading edge of the nearest rain cell to your location dot, labeled in minutes, on the map and on the widget alike.

ia.coreObject: The next two hours of sky over your exact location
ia.primaryLoop: Glance at the widget before stepping out; the map is only opened when you want to see the shape of what is coming.

weather-apps-7.territory: A storm has a name now and it's pointed at the person's zip code; family group chats are filling with contradictory screenshots and the TV is selling fear by the hour. The interface answers with civil-defense composure: a printed-bulletin calm that converts a swirling map into three times for your exact address — when it arrives, when it peaks, when it clears. No cinematics, no sirens, just the steadiness people borrow their courage from.

palette.note: Bulletin white with near-black text for maximum legibility on a dying phone in a dark house; storm indigo carries all data and wind fields, and a single warning crimson #D2232A appears only on active warning rows, never as decoration.

weather-apps-7.typography: IBM Plex Sans for guidance and IBM Plex Mono for times and wind speeds — the visual lineage of NWS teletype bulletins, redrawn at modern sizes with sentence-case calm.
weather-apps-7.motif: The arrival spine: one vertical hour-by-hour line per address, with three fixed stations — arrives, peaks, clears — that every map, model and alert hangs off of; the storm is always translated back onto this spine.

ia.coreObject: The address — a saved place with its own arrival spine for the active storm
ia.primaryLoop: During a storm, check the spine for each saved address a few times a day as forecasts shift; between storms the app stays silent, which is exactly why it's trusted when it speaks.

screens.title: Quiet — nothing to track
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state doubling as the product promise: silence when the tropics are silent.
screens.hero: A nearly blank page with a single status line and an add-address card
screens.data: 'No active storms in the Atlantic basin. Last advisory scan: today 06:00 ET. We'll stay quiet until there's something real.'; button 'Add the addresses you'd protect'

screens.title: Onboarding — your addresses

screens.data: 'Home — 1427 Mangrove Ln, Cape Coral, FL'; 'Dad — Charleston, SC'; 'Boat — Factory Bay Marina, Marco Island, FL'; note 'Each address gets its own arrival times. Free tier: 1 address.'

screens.title: Onboarding — when to speak up

weight-tracker-1.territory: Someone six weeks into a drug that costs more than their car payment: hopeful, slightly nauseous, and tired of juggling four apps to feel in control of one treatment. The interface answers with the steadiness of a well-run clinic binder: everything in its place on the ladder, numbers without judgement, and the calm assurance that nothing you log will ever be reset.

palette.note: Warm paper-white keeps months of data restful to read; the indigo marks exactly one thing, your current position on the ladder, so orientation is always a single saccade away.

weight-tracker-1.typography: Public Sans carries every number and label with civic plainness, while Fraunces appears only at ladder milestones and course events, giving the moments that matter a humane, unhurried voice.
weight-tracker-1.motif: The dose ladder rail: a single vertical stepped line that runs through the whole app, every screen pinning its content to a rung, so you always know where in the course you are standing.

ia.coreObject: The course: a dose ladder with every shot, side effect, and weigh-in pinned to its rungs
ia.primaryLoop: Log shot day and how you feel in under a minute, glance at where you stand on the ladder and what the next step holds; shot day itself brings them back every week.

screens.title: Your medication, your rung
screens.purpose: First onboarding step: pick the drug and current dose, with the full modern list present.
screens.hero: A medication list where oral Wegovy simply exists, no workaround needed
screens.data: Options: Ozempic, Wegovy (injection), Wegovy (oral, 25 mg), Mounjaro, Zepbound, compounded semaglutide. Selected: Mounjaro 5 mg, week 6. Starting weight field accepting 356.2 lb without complaint. Copy: 'Any weight, any dose, any form. The app adapts to your prescription, not the reverse.'

screens.title: Draw the ladder
screens.purpose: Second and last onboarding step: the proposed titration path, fully editable, doctor-first.
screens.hero: The ladder rail with rungs at standard step-up dates, each rung draggable
screens.data: Rungs: 2.5 mg (done, weeks 1-4), 5 mg (current, weeks 5-8), 7.5 mg (Jul 24), 10 mg (Aug 21), maintenance 10 mg (from Sep 18). Copy: 'Your doctor decides the steps. We just keep the map, and the map survives every change.'

screens.title: The ladder is waiting
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state: the course exists before the first entry, so day one feels anchored.
screens.hero: The full ladder drawn with today's rung glowing, no data pinned yet
screens.data: Copy: 'Your first entry anchors the ladder. Log this week's shot and today's weight, everything else attaches from there.' Button: 'Log first shot'. Sub: 'Takes about 40 seconds.'

screens.title: Week 6 of 5 mg
screens.purpose: The main screen mid-use: today's position on the ladder with the whole week's feed beside it.
screens.hero: The ladder rail down the left edge, current rung indigo, the day feed pinned to it
screens.data: Header: 'Week 6 of 5 mg · next review Jul 24'. Feed: 'Shot, right abdomen, Jul 9', 'Weight 348.6 lb (down 7.6 since start)', 'Protein 84 g of 120 g', 'Water 64 oz', 'Nausea, mild, morning'. Next-up chip: 'Shot day Thursday'.

screens.title: Where the needle goes
screens.purpose: Shot logging with site rotation, the mechanic that prevents tissue damage nobody warns you about.
screens.hero: A simple front/back body map with the last four sites stamped and faded by age
screens.data: History: left thigh Jul 4, right thigh Jun 27, left abdomen Jun 20. Suggested: 'right abdomen, rested 3 weeks'. Confirm button logs site, dose 5 mg, and time in one tap. Reminder note: 'Thursday 8 am, your schedule, not ours.'

screens.title: All of it, not one of it
screens.purpose: Multiple side effects per day, because bodies do not queue their symptoms.
screens.hero: A day card holding three symptom chips at different severities plus a free note
screens.data: Jul 10: 'Nausea, mild, morning', 'Constipation, moderate, day 3', 'Fatigue, mild, evening'. Note: 'Skipped dinner, sipped broth instead.' Each chip pinned to the 5 mg rung so patterns per dose become visible later.

screens.title: The doctor moved you early
screens.purpose: The dose-change event: a course event, not a broken app.
screens.hero: The ladder redrawing with a Fraunces-set event card at the change point
screens.data: Event: 'Jul 15 · moved to 7.5 mg two weeks early, per Dr. Malhotra'. Below: 'Your ladder updated. Reminders re-anchored to Thursday. Nothing was reset, weeks 1-6 stay exactly where they were.' Old plan shown as a faint ghost rail beside the new one.

screens.title: Switching to the pill
screens.purpose: Form change handled as a first-class course event, same course, same history.
screens.hero: The ladder continuing seamlessly from an injection rung to an oral rung
screens.data: Event: 'Aug 2 · switched to oral Wegovy 25 mg daily'. Ladder legend updates: syringe glyph becomes tablet glyph from this rung on. Site rotation quietly retires. Copy: 'One course, two forms. Your trend line never blinks.'

screens.title: Weight against the rungs
screens.purpose: The trend view: weight overlaid on dose steps, with the plateau treated as expected terrain.
screens.hero: A 20-week weight line with dose steps shaded as bands behind it
screens.data: Line: 356.2 lb (week 1) to 341.0 lb (week 20), visibly flattening across weeks 17-20. Annotation in Fraunces: 'Plateaus are part of the ladder. Your maintenance review is in 3 weeks.' Bands labeled 2.5 mg, 5 mg, 7.5 mg. Side-effect density dots run beneath the axis.

screens.title: The appointment sheet
screens.purpose: The doctor report: the whole course compressed into pages a clinician will actually read.
screens.hero: A PDF preview titled with patient name and date range
screens.data: Range: May 29 – Oct 8. Page 1: dose ladder with actual dates and the early step-up flagged. Page 2: weight trend by dose band. Page 3: side effects grouped by dose (nausea faded after week 2 of each step). Page 4: injection site log. Button: 'Share before Thursday's appointment'.

screens.title: New phone, whole history
screens.purpose: Data transfer that survives even an iPhone-to-Android move, the loss that makes payers angriest.
screens.hero: A single course file being handed between two phone outlines
screens.data: Button: 'Export course file (.glp, 148 KB, encrypted)'. Copy: 'Everything: ladder, shots, symptoms, weights, events. Import on any phone, iPhone or Android, and the ladder redraws identically.' Last backup stamp: 'auto-backed up today, 6:12 am'.

screens.title: The log is free, the ladder is Pro
screens.purpose: The paywall, honest about what stays free forever and priced as pocket change next to the drug.
screens.hero: A split card: the free column fully lit, no padlock on the shot log
screens.data: 'Free forever: shot log, site rotation, weight tracking. That promise does not expire.' Pro, $29/year: the dose ladder, multi-symptom tracking, dose-change events, the doctor report. Copy: 'Your medication costs hundreds a month. Pro costs $2.40 of it.' Buttons: 'Start Pro', 'Restore purchase', 'Keep free plan'. No trial timers, no locked past data.

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: Units, reminders, medications, and the privacy posture health data demands.
screens.hero: The reminder schedule block first, because shot day is the heartbeat
screens.data: Reminder: Thursday 8 am, snooze respects your morning. Units: lb / kg (accepts any value). Medication list managed here, including compounded. Privacy: 'Health data stays on device and in your encrypted backup, never sold, no ad SDKs.' Export: course file, CSV. Delete everything.

workout-fitness-1.territory: The lifter is standing at the bench between warmup and first set, chalk on hands, rest timer in their head, and the only question is what did I do last Tuesday. The interface answers with iron-room directness: dark like the gym floor, numbers big as plates, and last session's weights already on screen before the first rep, so momentum never waits on a menu. Heat lives in the accent, not in decoration.

palette.note: Iron and chalk carry the whole screen; the volt yellow strikes only on the active set, the running rest timer, and a new personal best, one hot mark per screen like tape on a barbell.

workout-fitness-1.typography: Barlow Condensed in bold for exercise names, stacked tight like plates on a bar, with Roboto Mono tabular for every weight and rep so 82.5 x 5 aligns into columns you can read from arm's length.
workout-fitness-1.motif: The ghost row: today's empty set inputs are printed over a faint imprint of the exact numbers from your last session, so logging feels like overwriting last week in chalk rather than filling a blank form.

ia.coreObject: The set (exercise, weight, reps, note) inside a session, backed by every prior session of that exercise
ia.primaryLoop: Open today's split, see last session's numbers under each exercise, beat or match them set by set in two taps, and leave with the whole history still yours.

screens.title: Pick your split
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 1: choose or sketch the weekly structure so day one starts inside a plan.
screens.hero: Three big split cards in condensed caps.
screens.data: Upper / Lower, 4 days. Push Pull Legs, 6 days. Start from blank. Units toggle: kg selected. Selected card shows Day 1: Upper A with Bench, Row, OHP, Curl.

screens.title: Bring your history
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 2: import the old log so years of numbers survive the switch, the fear this app exists to kill.
screens.hero: A drop zone shaped like a CSV file with recognized-app chips.
screens.data: Import from: Hevy CSV, Strong CSV, generic CSV. Preview after pick: 214 workouts, 1,842 sets, Mar 2024 to Jul 2026, all exercises matched. Buttons: Import everything · Start fresh instead.

screens.title: Nothing behind you yet
screens.purpose: First-launch empty state for the fresh starter: the ghost rows exist but are honestly empty.
screens.hero: The logging table with blank ghost rows and one line of promise.
screens.data: Barbell Bench Press. Ghost area reads: No last session yet. After tonight, your numbers will be waiting here. Button: Start Upper A.

screens.title: Train, mid-set
screens.purpose: Main screen mid-use: the core promise on screen, last five sessions visible before the first set is logged.

screens.data: Barbell Bench Press. Last time, Jul 8: 80x5, 80x5, 80x4, note 'felt heavy'. Strip behind it: Jul 4, Jul 1, Jun 27, Jun 24. Today: set 1 done 82.5x5 in volt, set 2 active with rest timer 1:32 counting, sets 3 and 4 as ghost rows reading 80x5.

screens.title: Change it once
screens.purpose: The edit-once mechanic at its moment: bump the weight on set one and every remaining set updates itself.
screens.hero: A weight stepper on set 1 with the lower sets visibly rewriting.
screens.data: Set 1 changed 80 to 82.5 with the +2.5 stepper. Sets 2 to 4 flip from 80 to 82.5 in one beat with a small caption: applied to remaining sets. Undo chip stays for 5 seconds.

screens.title: Five sessions deep
screens.purpose: The history strip expanded: the full recent picture of one lift without leaving the logging screen.
screens.hero: Five compact session columns side by side, newest on the right.
screens.data: Bench Press. Jun 24: 77.5x5,5,5. Jun 27: 80x5,4,4. Jul 1: 80x5,5,4. Jul 4: 80x5,5,5. Jul 8: 80x5,5,4 with note 'felt heavy'. Best set ever pinned above: 90x2 on May 12. One line: swipe for the full year.

screens.title: Phone in the locker
screens.purpose: The watch mechanic: a full set logged from the wrist with no phone in range.
screens.hero: A watch face mock with one exercise, one weight, one big log button.
screens.data: Watch shows: Incline DB Press, set 3 of 4, 30 kg x 8, ghost under it 30x8 last time. Buttons: Done · +2.5 · -2.5. Rest ring counting 1:10. Corner glyph: standalone, phone not connected.

screens.title: The session never breaks
screens.purpose: The reconnect state: watch-logged sets merge back when the phone returns, shown plainly so trust is earned, not assumed.
screens.hero: A quiet merge banner over the finished session, no spinner theater.
screens.data: Banner: 9 sets recorded on watch merged into tonight's session. 0 duplicates, 0 lost. Session total: Upper A, 52 min, 21 sets, 6,420 kg volume. Tap to review the merged rows, each tagged with a small watch glyph.

screens.title: Programs

screens.hero: Folder rows in condensed caps with day chips.
screens.data: Folder: Strength Block 3, days Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B. Folder: Meet Prep (archived). Reorder handle on each row. Footer: next up tomorrow, Lower A, last done Jul 9.

screens.title: Pay for the log, keep the data
screens.purpose: The paywall in plain iron-room language: yearly or lifetime, with the export promise repeated right on the price card.
screens.hero: Two price plates side by side like weight plates, lifetime slightly larger.
screens.data: $10 / year or $30 lifetime. Copy: Ghost rows, watch logging, unlimited programs. Your history exports free forever either way, paid or not. Buttons: Get lifetime $30 · Yearly $10 · Restore purchase. Footnote: less than one month of gym dues.

screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: The utility drawer: units, bar math, backups, and the exits kept honest.
screens.hero: A grouped dark list with units on top.
screens.data: Units: kg. Default bar: 20 kg. Rest timer: 2:00, auto-start on. Watch: standalone logging on. Backup: on-device plus iCloud, last backup today 06:40. Export CSV. Import CSV. Restore purchase.

workout-fitness-2.territory: She is standing at the bench between sets, phone in chalky hands, and the question is never motivation, it is a number: what do I put on the bar right now. The interface answers with loud, certain type and heat: the weight in huge digits, the history right under her thumb, and the promise that hitting today's sets makes next session heavier. Momentum you can read from three feet away.

palette.note: Ember orange marks exactly one thing: forward load progression, so every +2.5 lb chip, every history uptick, and the finish state burn, while everything static stays black on gym-chalk white.

workout-fitness-2.typography: Druk Wide slams the working weight and rep targets into poster-size certainty readable mid-set; Graphik handles coaching lines and history in a calm counterweight.
workout-fitness-2.motif: The plate ledger: every exercise carries a rising stack of plate-shaped bars, one per session, so months of training read as iron physically piling up, and today's suggested weight always sits on top of the stack.

ia.coreObject: The working set: an exercise, its prescribed weight and reps today, backed by its full plate-ledger history
ia.primaryLoop: Train 2–4 times a week following the day's card, log each set with one tap, and come back because completing all sets visibly loads the next session heavier.

screens.title: Onboarding — pick your style

screens.title: Train with the plan

workout-fitness-3.territory: You walk into the gym at 6:40 am with chalk on your hands and zero appetite for arithmetic. The interface answers like a rack card already filled in by a coach who did the math last night: heavy, certain, one number at a time. Heat lives in the numbers, not in confetti.

palette.note: The screen stays cast-iron matte; the ember orange is spent only on the one number you lift next and on the deload rule when it fires.

workout-fitness-3.typography: Druk Condensed carries the loaded weight in poster sizes, IBM Plex Mono sets the set-and-rep grids like a training log stamped in steel, and nothing is ever italic.
workout-fitness-3.motif: The plate stack: every weight is drawn as its actual per-side plate loadout, thin colored slabs against the bar, so 225 lb is never an abstract number but two 45s hanging on each side.

ia.coreObject: The session: a pre-calculated card of lifts with exact weight, sets and reps derived from your last logged session
ia.primaryLoop: Open the app at the rack, lift what the card says, tap each set done or missed, and tomorrow's math is already settled before you leave the floor.

workout-fitness-4.territory: A 45-year-old with a bad left knee walks into training carrying two feelings at once: the drive to still be strong and the memory of the last time a workout set them back three weeks. The interface answers with the focused heat of a well-run gym at night — bold, warm, full of momentum — but with a guardrail always visible: your marked zones are drawn on every screen, and nothing the app hands you touches them.

palette.note: Warm charcoal like a gym after hours with ember orange for effort and momentum, while the protected body zones are always rendered in a cool guarded blue (#5B8DBE) so heat and caution never share a color.

workout-fitness-4.typography: Druk Wide for session headers and load numbers, Graphik for exercise names and coaching notes; the condensed shouting is reserved for effort, the talking voice for safety.
workout-fitness-4.motif: The guarded silhouette: a small body outline that lives in the corner of every screen with your marked zones shaded cool blue, and every exercise card carries the same silhouette showing exactly which joints it loads.

ia.coreObject: The plan-around: a training program generated from the restriction outward, where marked body zones filter every exercise before it ever reaches you
ia.primaryLoop: Open today's session built around your map, train, answer one question about how the zone felt, and watch the trend earn back the movements pain took away.

screens.title: Mark what hurts
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 1: the body map is the first screen because the restriction is the product's starting point.
screens.hero: A full-height front/back body silhouette; tapped zones shade cool blue with a severity slider each
screens.data: Marked: 'Left knee — flares on impact and deep bends', 'Lower back — no loaded flexion'. Slider labels: 'twinges / hurts under load / avoid entirely'. Footer: 'Not rehab, not diagnosis. We build workouts that stay out of these zones.'

screens.title: What you're working with
screens.purpose: Onboarding step 2: goal, days, and equipment, then the plan proves itself by counting what fits.
screens.hero: Three quick pickers resolving into a live counter of safe exercises
screens.data: 'Goal: keep strength · 3 days/week · Dumbbells + bench at home'. Counter fills: '412 exercises in library → 176 fit your map'. Button: 'Build my first week'. Note: 'Every one of the 176 is tagged by knee, lumbar, shoulder, and wrist demand.'

screens.title: Today: Lower body, knee-guarded
screens.purpose: Main screen mid-session: the workout underway, each movement showing what it spares as prominently as what it builds.
screens.hero: The current exercise card with the guarded silhouette confirming both blue zones untouched
screens.data: 'Session 2 of 3 · week 6'. Current: 'Box squat to 16-inch bench · 3×8 · 2×20 lb dumbbells — builds quads and glutes, keeps the knee above 90°'. Up next: 'Hip thrust 3×10', 'Standing calf raise 3×15'. Rest timer: '1:30'. Corner silhouette: left knee and lower back shaded blue, unloaded.

screens.title: Swap in one gesture
screens.purpose: The swap mechanic: slide an exercise away and see precisely what the replacement protects.
screens.hero: A card mid-swipe revealing the alternative beneath, with a one-line protection note bridging them
screens.data: Swiping away: 'Romanian deadlift'. Revealed: 'Hip thrust — same glute work, zero spinal shear'. Second option on further swipe: 'Cable pull-through — hinge pattern, load stays low'. Each alternative carries its own mini silhouette.

screens.title: Honest filters
screens.purpose: The library filter view where the pre-tagged taxonomy earns its keep: filters that mean what they say.
screens.hero: Three large toggle chips over the live-filtering exercise grid
screens.data: Toggles on: 'Standing only', 'No jumping', 'No wrist loading'. Grid updates: '176 → 61 exercises'. Sample cards: 'Landmine press — wrists neutral', 'Step-back lunge — no impact', 'Farmer carry — grip yes, wrist bend no'. Each card shows its joint-demand row.

screens.title: Read the fine print on a movement
screens.purpose: Exercise detail with the joint-demand meter, the trust anchor for someone burned by generic plans.
screens.hero: The exercise demo with a four-row demand meter below: knees, lumbar, shoulders, wrists
screens.data: 'Goblet squat'. Meter: 'Knees: moderate — capped depth variant available · Lumbar: low · Shoulders: low · Wrists: low'. Note: 'With your map, we serve the box variant by default.' Buttons: 'Use box variant', 'Exclude this movement entirely'.

screens.title: One question after
screens.purpose: Post-session check-in: a single tap on how the zone felt, feeding the trend that drives the whole plan.
screens.hero: The guarded silhouette enlarged, left knee pulsing softly, three big answer chips
screens.data: 'Session done: 34 min, 8 exercises. How did the left knee feel?' Chips: 'Better than usual / Same / Worse'. Below, last week's answers as small dots: 'Better · Same · Better'. Nothing else asked.

screens.title: Eight weeks of the knee
screens.purpose: The trend chart translating check-ins into the only progress this user truly wants: less pain under more work.
screens.hero: A dual-line chart: knee-feel trend rising over training volume bars
screens.data: 'Left knee · 8 weeks · 21 sessions'. Trend: 'Worse ×2 in week 1 → Better ×3 in week 8'. Volume line: 'weekly sets 9 → 14'. Caption in plain words: 'You're doing 55% more work and the knee reports better. That's the whole game.'

screens.title: Earning one back
screens.purpose: The reintroduction moment: the plan proposes returning a removed movement, gently and reversibly.
screens.hero: An exercise card sliding from the blue 'set aside' shelf toward the active plan, at half opacity
screens.data: '3 weeks of "better" on the left knee. Ready to try step-ups again?' Terms stated: 'Half volume: 2×6, 6-inch box, last slot in Friday's session. One "worse" and it goes back on the shelf, no argument.' Buttons: 'Try it Friday', 'Not yet'.

screens.title: Flare-up protocol
screens.purpose: The conflict state: two 'worse' reports trigger an automatic retreat, shown before today's session starts.
screens.hero: The silhouette with the left knee zone expanded and today's revised session beside it
screens.data: 'You marked "worse" twice this week. Today drops all knee loading — upper body and hinge-free core instead: Floor press 3×10, Seated row 3×12, Pallof press 3×10/side.' Footer: 'The knee work waits. It doesn't disappear.' Link: 'If pain persists, see a professional — we only route around, we don't treat.'

screens.title: Training that won't set you back

Straight talk: 'A single physio visit runs $90+. This isn't physio — it's every workout not making things worse.' Links: 'Restore purchase', 'Continue free: 1 guarded session per week'.

workout-fitness-5.territory: A 68-year-old in her living room at nine in the morning, a little stiff, quietly worried about what she can't do anymore. The interface answers with respect instead of cheer: big calm type, a chair treated as equipment rather than a concession, and progress measured in what her Tuesday actually needs — standing at the sink, stairs without the rail.

palette.note: One quiet capability-green marks the chosen level and 'you did it' moments; nothing flashes, nothing counts down in red.

workout-fitness-5.typography: Atkinson Hyperlegible for everything with a 20pt floor, and Recoleta only on session names to keep the warmth of a printed community-center flyer.
workout-fitness-5.motif: The three-chair dial: every exercise carries the same trio of chair glyphs (seated, hand on chair, chair pushed away), and picking your level is turning that dial, session after session.

ia.coreObject: Session
ia.primaryLoop: Show up three mornings a week, turn the chair dial to how today feels, and finish in about 25 minutes without ever getting on the floor.

workout-fitness-6.territory: The trainer is between sessions with twenty minutes and a client roster on their mind; their client is under a bar in a basement gym with no signal. Both arrive needing a tool that simply holds. The interface answers like a well-organized workbench: bold, fast, physical, with the heat of the gym in its type but none of the marketplace noise. Reliability is the aesthetic.

palette.note: Chalk-and-concrete neutrals keep long working sessions calm while the hot orange-red hits only on PRs, flags, and the active set, like tape on a barbell.

workout-fitness-6.typography: Archivo Black for exercise names and client headers with Inter for logs and numbers in tabular figures; the loud condensed headers carry the gym's energy while the log stays as legible as a spreadsheet.
workout-fitness-6.motif: The tally row: every set ever logged renders as a horizontal row of filled weight-plate ticks (4×6 = four thick ticks), a mark-making language that turns each program and history view into chalk tallies on a rack.

ia.coreObject: The program: a week-by-day grid of exercises with sets, loads, and the trainer's own video cues, mirrored by the client's set log
ia.primaryLoop: Clients log sets during every workout, and the trainer sweeps the roster once or twice a day to review logs, drop comments on specific sets, and adjust next week's loads, which is the working rhythm the whole business runs on.

workout-fitness-8.territory: 5:50am, garage treadmill, one lamp on, earbuds in before the house wakes. The person is half-asleep and needs momentum handed to them by a voice, not a screen. The interface answers as a dark, warm control room: everything designed to be heard, and the few things shown legible in one glance from a moving belt.

palette.note: The screen stays embers-dark because the product lives in your ears; rose heat ignites only on the current push interval and cools to gray as you recover.

workout-fitness-8.typography: Druk Condensed for the giant pace and interval numbers read off a moving belt, Graphik for everything the trainer would say out loud.
workout-fitness-8.motif: The cue strip: every class is a horizontal cadence ribbon of fine ticks, and the trainer's upcoming voice cues glow as taller rose ticks, so you can see the push coming before you hear it.

ia.coreObject: Class
